Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 45, verses 1–2:

This surah is also among the Ḥawāmīm, the surahs that open with the words of the Exalted, (Ḥā Mīm). We have already discussed them, but since God has repeated them, we must also address them with what God opens to us, and this will not be considered repetition.

When we look at the life we see, we find a visible dominion (mulk mushahad) and an unseen kingdom (malakut ghayr mushahad). Everything that is hidden from your senses is the unseen (ghayb), which no one knows except God. Take the creed and the acts of worship as examples: you will find that they rest on these two sides, the unseen (al-ghayb) and the seen (al-mashhad).

By reason you can demonstrate the oneness of God, His existence, and that He is the Creator of this whole universe. Man came into this universe and found it as it is now: the sun, the moon and the stars, the heavens and the earth, water and air.

Therefore no one has claimed that he created it. The Exalted said: ﴿And if you asked them, "Who created the heavens and the earth?" they would surely say, "God..."﴾ [Luqman: 25] and He said: ﴿And if you asked them, "Who created them?" they would surely say, "God..."﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 87].

This is the seen. In the creed there are other matters that are unseen, which we believe in because God has informed us of them, such as the matters of the Hereafter, the resurrection, the reckoning, Paradise and Hell. Take for example prayer among the acts of worship: we can understand rational reasons for it, so we say: God prescribed it for us five times a day and night so that the servant may keep returning to his Creator, that he may draw strength and help from Him, that he may find intimacy in meeting Him, and that he may take from the overflow of His bounty and its illuminations.

Prayer also makes the servants equal, the rich and the poor, the leader and the led; all prostrate to God. This is a servitude-based pathway through the universe. All of this is the seen. But by God, tell me: why was the dawn prayer two rak'ahs, the noon prayer four, and the sunset prayer three? These are the unseen, which we believe in as they are, as the Messenger of God, the trustworthy one over the law of God, informed us.

Likewise, in the Noble Qur'an there is the unseen and the seen. The unseen is in these disjoined letters (al-huruf al-muqatta'a), whose meaning God has reserved knowledge of, while the rest of the Qur'an is seen, because it is clear, its meaning manifest and its purpose evident, since the Exalted wants to make us worship through the unseen just as He made us worship through the seen.

The unseen is the locus of faith. As for the seen, it is not a sphere for faith or disbelief. So do not say, for example, "I believe that the sun is rising," but say, "I believe in the Last Day."

So His saying here, (Ḥā Mīm), means: disjoined letters at the beginning of some surahs of the Qur'an, which are unseen; we believe in them and leave their meaning to their Sender, the Exalted. ﴿The revelation of the Book...﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 2] This is the seen. In the surah before it, (Ḥā Mīm) is unseen, and ﴿and the clear Book﴾ [al-Dukhan: 2] is seen. ﴿Indeed, We sent it down in a blessed night...﴾ [al-Dukhan: 3] meaning: both the unseen and the seen are sent down from God, so they are equal in worshipping God, the Exalted. Just as He made you worship through what is clear and understood, He made you worship through the unseen that you do not comprehend. All that remains is that we circle around them, trying to draw out some of their secrets.

Therefore we say that the whole Qur'an is built on wasl (continuity/connection) among its verses and among its surahs, to the extent that the last word of surah al-Nas is connected to the first word of al-Fatihah, so we say: ﴿from the jinn and mankind. In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds﴾, and so on.

Therefore we call the reciter of the Qur'an "al-ḥall al-murtaḥil" (the one who alights and departs), meaning: he hardly finishes the Qur'an before he begins again from its beginning.

As for the disjoined letters at the beginnings of surahs, they are built on waqf (pausing). You say: Ḥā, Mīm, Alif Lām Mīm, whereas you do not pause on the same letters in ﴿Did We not expand for you your breast?﴾ [al-Sharh: 1].

So: every pronunciation has a reason and has secrets. It is like the teeth of a key that opens for you: a key that opens for you with one tooth, a key that opens for you with two, and a key that opens for you with three.

His saying: ﴿from God, the Mighty, the Wise﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 2] chose here the name al-'Azīz, because the Qur'an will be sent down and you will find among the people those who deny it, so do not concern yourself with that, and do not let their denial deceive you. God, who sends down this Book, is Mighty and cannot be overcome, and this might is not by compulsion, but is a might with wisdom. ﴿al-Ḥakīm﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 2]: the Wise is the one who places a thing in its appropriate place.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 45, verse 3:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, in the heavens and the earth..﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 3]. He made the heavens and the earth a container (ẓarf), so do not look at the heavens and the earth in their essence, but look at the signs (āyāt) and secrets contained in them. They are full of signs which Allah reveals in their time, and whenever minds open and sciences develop, a sign of Allah's signs in the heavens and the earth becomes apparent to us.

Consider, for example, the revolution in the field of communications, and the vibrations and broadcasts in the air (for television), yet they do not mix or overlap. Consider the vast space and what mankind has reached in conquering space, launching ships and rockets that reach other planets, settle on them, and send us images from them. All of these are signs of Allah's signs which He, glorified is He, reveals to us in its appropriate time.

So: the signs of Allah are numerous in the heavens and the earth, and even beneath the earth. Therefore Allah bestows His blessings upon us, saying: ﴿To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth and whatever is between them and whatever is beneath the soil.﴾ [Ta-Ha: 6].

Therefore our master ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud said: "Athīrū al-Qur'ān," meaning "stir it up" (haiyijūhu), like the earth when we plough it to take out what is in it of goodness. Likewise, everything attributed to Allah, the Exalted, contains countless treasures of good.

If the heavens and the earth are a container, we may ask: which is more precious, the container or what is contained in it? Is the letter or message more precious, or the envelope in which it is placed? The treasury or what is placed in it is more precious.

Likewise the heavens and the earth, despite their greatness and strength, what is in them of signs and wonders is greater and more precious than them. Therefore you remember that we have forbidden placing anything between the pages of the Mushaf. Why? So that the Book of Allah, the Exalted, does not become a container for anything, no matter how dear and precious it is to you, because the Qur'an is more precious and dearer than anything else, so do not make it a container for anything.

And His saying: ﴿for signs for the believers﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 3]. Āyāt is the plural of āyah (sign), which is a thing that reaches the furthest degree of beauty, as we say: so-and-so is an āyah in beauty, or in eloquence, or in generosity. So āyah means a wondrous thing in its field.

We have explained that the word āyah is used in three meanings: cosmic signs that establish the power of the Creator, glorified is He, and His wisdom: ﴿And among His signs are the night and the day and the sun and the moon..﴾ [Fussilat: 37].

If a thing is unique in being a wondrous thing indicating power, it is called an āyah on its own. Among this is His saying: ﴿And We made the night and the day two signs..﴾ [al-Isra': 12], so each of them is an āyah on its own.

He said concerning ʿIsa son of Maryam, peace be upon him, and his mother Maryam: ﴿And We made the son of Maryam and his mother a sign..﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 50]. So they are one sign, because the aspect of wonder in them is one, and the common element between them in miraculousness is one matter, so they were one sign.

Then after that come miraculous signs (āyāt muʿjizāt) which accompany the messengers to support them and establish the truth of their conveying from Allah, such as the staff of Musa and the she-camel of Salih.

Then the third type of signs is the signs of the Wise Reminder in the Noble Qur'an, and they call them "bearers of rulings" (ḥāmilat al-aḥkām).

So the meaning of: ﴿for signs for the believers﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 3] is: O believers in me, pay attention to these signs so that you may convince others who have not believed among the disbelievers and the atheists. Therefore we sit (nunādī, i.e., we call out) among them and say to them: look at this, look at that, reflect upon the power of Allah in this and that.

This is our mission: to call people, and to guide them to Allah by what? By His signs in the cosmos. Therefore our Lord, glorified is He, teaches us how to guide people by the signs, saying: ﴿And among His signs are the night and the day and the sun and the moon. Do not prostrate to the sun or to the moon, but prostrate to Allah who created them, if it is Him that you worship.﴾ [Fussilat: 37].

That is: do not let the greatness of these signs deceive you; their Creator is greater, and He who created beauty is more beautiful than beauty. Beware lest your admiration for the night, the day, the sun and the moon turn you away from their Creator. He is the one deserving of worship, not they. This means that the Creator, glorified is He, is keen on His handiwork, keen on guiding people and saving them from what would destroy them.

It is as though this verse says to the believers in Allah: these cosmic signs were made by Allah so that they may convince you first, and then you convince others with them.

Therefore, if we look at the scholars of religion and the scholars of nature in the fields of humans, animals, plants and inanimate things, we find that the scholars of nature are ahead, because the scholars of religion explain to people the lawful and the unlawful, proceeding first from faith in Allah. The explanation of rulings is a branch of faith. So contemplation of cosmic signs and inference from them to their Creator, mighty and majestic is He, is more important.

Among the wonders of Allah's craftsmanship in His creation: in the late 1920s they said that the seven heavens are the seven planets that revolve around the sun, and in the year after that they discovered another planet, until their number reached ten, then they discovered Venus, and thus all the old theories changed.

Among the wonders of creation in these planets: we know that the day is shorter in time than the year, because the day is 1/365 of the year. After we came to know the science of solid geometry, we found Venus, which is the second star after the sun, and before it Mercury.

Strangely, they found that the day of Venus is longer than the year of Venus. Our day is the rotation of the earth around itself, and the year is its revolution around the sun. When they observed the day of Venus by measuring it against the day of the earth, they found that the day is longer than the year: the day of Venus is 244 earth days, and the year is 225 earth days.

This is correct, because the direction is separate. Each star has its own motion, and this motion may be rapid in its rotation around itself and slow in its revolution around the sun, or the reverse, and from here the difference arises. There is no obstacle to the day being longer than the year. The last of these planets, Pluto, they found that its day equals 6.5 earth days, and its year 268 earth days.

From this we understand the power of the Creator, glorified is He, and that this universe was created with precision and perfection, not by chance, and not merely as a monotonous system like rigid moulds, but as absolute power and self-subsistence that moves this universe and manages it with complete precision and perfection.

Then if a person looks into himself, he would find another world full of signs. Look at people and the difference of their languages, dialects, constitutions and fingerprints: ﴿And among His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the difference of your tongues and your colours. Indeed in that are signs for those of knowledge.﴾ [al-Rum: 22].

Had He willed, He would have made us of one colour and one tongue, but from His wisdom, the Exalted, in creation is that He unites you with others in a common matter, then distinguishes you from them by another matter entirely different.

We used to know, in distinguishing between people, the fingerprint. Now they have found a voiceprint, a jawprint, and a scent print. All these prints distinguish the human being, meaning that they are not repeated in another person despite the large number of people. Is this not a wondrous miracle of creation that calls us to faith in the Creator, majestic and exalted is He?

We have said: among the wonders of creation in the human body is that no conduction of heat occurs in it as occurs in other bodies. The normal body temperature is 37 degrees, and you find it in a human at the equator and in a human at the frozen pole, because the body retains this degree within itself. Then every organ of the body has its appropriate temperature so that it can perform its task.

So you will be amazed when you learn that the eye's temperature does not exceed 9 degrees, while the liver's temperature is not less than 40 degrees, and they are in one connected body, yet no heat conduction occurs in it, so that the heat of the liver does not pass to the heat of the eye, for example.

Therefore, just as Islam was concerned with legislating the lawful and the unlawful and explaining them to people, it was even more concerned with explaining Allah's cosmic signs in all kinds of creatures: human, animal, plant and inanimate.

And read, if you wish: ﴿Have you not seen that Allah sends down water from the sky, and We bring forth thereby fruits of varying colours? And among the mountains are streaks, white and red, of varying colours, and jet-black. And among men and beasts and cattle are those of varying colours. Thus only those of His servants who have knowledge fear Allah. Indeed Allah is Mighty, Forgiving.﴾ [Fatir: 27-28].

Is there here a legal ruling about prayer, pilgrimage or fasting? All of it is a call to look and to reflect upon the cosmos. The scholars here are the scholars of the cosmos, not the scholars of religion. They are the people most knowing of Allah's signs, and they are the people most knowing of Allah and the most fearful of Him. Why?

Because they have stood upon His signs themselves, so they are the most knowing of them. Therefore religion has never neglected any science, because science serves the matter of faith and the matter of monotheism.

The Truth, glorified and exalted is He, gives us in the Qur'an all these examples so that we may take from them evidence of His existence, and take from them the attributes of dominance, wisdom, might and mercy, etc. Indeed, from the cosmic signs we take what makes our life upright and what corrects our concepts about things.

For example, take the relationship of man and woman. Some see that man is against woman, and that they are on opposite poles, so we hear the partisans of women and those of men facing them as if it were a battle. Yet when we read the Qur'an we find the saying of the Exalted: ﴿By the night when it covers, and by the day when it shines forth, and by Him who created the male and the female, indeed your efforts are diverse.﴾ [al-Layl: 1-4].

So opposite created things do not mean that they are contradictory. Beware of thinking that night is the opposite of day. Yes, it corresponds to it in the nature of things, but it does not oppose it. Night supports day and helps it, and day supports night and helps it; they are complementary. Night is for rest and day is for work, and each is important to the other, and each has a task and a role in life.

Likewise is the case with male and female. Therefore this cosmic sign teaches us a lesson in our social life: there is no need for all this clamour about the relationship between man and woman. Return to the Qur'an, for in it is healing, and in it are solutions to all our problems.

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿And in your creation and what He scatters abroad...﴾.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 45, verse 4:

The Qur'anic context here moves us from contemplating the signs of the heavens and the earth to contemplating our own selves, as He, glorified is He, said: ﴿And in your own selves. Will you not then see?﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 21]. The evidence for the Supreme Existence is not confined to the signs of the heavens and the earth. The miraculous nature is in the atom just as it is in the galaxy, and in the human body and its organs there are signs and wonders.

The poet expressed this when he said:

You think you are a small body,
Yet within you the greatest universe is folded.

The word ﴿creation (khalq) of you..﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 4]: when you hear the word khalq, you understand from it bringing into existence from nothing. The thing was non-existent and then God brought it into being. Khalq is not applied to the event itself but to the created thing; therefore He, exalted is He, said: ﴿This is the creation of God, so show me what those besides Him have created..﴾ [Luqman: 11]. So the meaning of khalq here is "creature" (makhluq). And it has the meaning of the act (of creating) in ﴿what those besides Him have created..﴾ [Luqman: 11].

So His saying: ﴿And in your creation..﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 4], i.e., among the cosmic signs is your creation, that is, the human beings. The process of creation has stages, those through which our master Adam passed, when he did not exist and God brought him into being from nothing. He was clay, then He shaped him, and breathed into him the spirit, so life stirred in him and he became a human being. Then He made his offspring after him through the pairing of male and female.

Thus, in our creation there are two stages: the stage of the first creation of our father Adam, and the stage of dispersal and spreading through reproduction. Therefore He, glorified is He, said in another verse: ﴿O mankind, fear your Lord, who created you from one soul and created from it its mate and dispersed from both of them many men and women..﴾ [al-Nisa': 1].

Thus, for us there is creation from nothing and there is bath (dispersal), i.e., spreading, and proliferation through reproduction. As for the animals (dawab), only the stage of dispersal is mentioned concerning them: ﴿and what He disperses of living creatures (dabbah)..﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 4], i.e., spreads. So where is the stage of their creation?

Firstly: the dabbah is everything that crawls on the earth other than man. In the language there is a style of expression they call (al-ihtibak) (interlocking, a figure in which two elements mutually complete each other), which is a branch of rhetoric known to specialists in it.

Al-ihtibak is that in speech there are two things, one of which clarifies the other and dispenses with it. The clearest example of this in the Qur'an is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿There has already been for you a sign in the two armies which met: one fighting in the cause of God and another disbelieving..﴾ [Al 'Imran: 13].

His saying ﴿and another disbelieving..﴾ [Al 'Imran: 13] indicates that the first is believing, i.e., a believing group fighting in the cause of God, and another, disbelieving, fighting in the cause of Satan. The mentioned part indicates the omitted part by contrast.

So the meaning in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and in your creation and what He disperses of living creatures (dabbah)﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 4] is that He mentioned creation in the first and omitted dispersal, and mentioned dispersal in the second and omitted creation. Accordingly the meaning is: and in your creation and what is dispersed of you, and in the creation of animals and what is dispersed of them.

﴿Signs for a people who are certain.﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 4]. The Truth, glorified is He, has informed us of the manner of the first creation from nothing through His creating Adam, and has told us of the stages of this creation until Adam became a complete human being who moves and walks upon the earth. He did not mention the details of the creation of others, so that we might analogize on what we have come to know.

When He spoke of Eve He said: ﴿who created you from one soul and created from it its mate..﴾ [al-Nisa': 1], meaning: in its manner. Likewise He did not speak of the creation of animals, because it is measured by the creation of Adam.

There is no doubt that whoever reflects on the creation of man and animals finds many signs and miracles indicating the absoluteness of the Creator's power, glorified is He. In the first creation there is absoluteness of power, for He created from nothing and without any prior model. He brought Adam into being without a father and without a mother, then created Eve from him, so she was from a father without a mother, and He created Jesus, peace be upon him, from a mother without a father, and He created the general run of creation from a father and a mother.

Thus, the absoluteness of power has encompassed every rational possibility of the matter, even if only once, so that the proof and the miracle might occur, and so that the Truth might establish itself for Himself, glorified is He: ﴿His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is.﴾ [Ya-Sin: 82].

And he who possesses giving possesses withholding. The motives for creation and procreation may be present, yet it does not happen: ﴿He bestows female [children] upon whom He wills and bestows male [children] upon whom He wills. Or He weds them [both] males and females, and He renders whom He wills barren..﴾ [al-Shura: 49-50].

And you know from the story of our master Zakariyya, peace be upon him, how he did not beget children until he reached old age, and his wife was barren, so that he despaired of this matter. When God willed that he should beget, He made the causes subservient to him, gave him the good news of a son, and also named him for him.

All these are signs of creation, and they are many and extended. In every stage of them there is a miracle and power, beginning with the meeting between husband and wife and the union of the male sperm cell with the female ovum. If the fertilization of the ovum is accomplished, pregnancy occurs, and the blood is transformed into nourishment for the fetus, which is its provision until it is born. If pregnancy does not occur, this blood is discharged during the period of menstruation.

This means that the Creator, glorified is He, when He creates the human being, creates with him his provision. The fetus is not nourished by the food of its mother but by its own special nourishment, as is shown by the fact that the mother does not benefit from this blood if no pregnancy occurs.

His saying, glorified is He: ﴿Signs for a people who are certain.﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 4]. Certainty (yaqin) is faith and firm conviction settled in the heart, such that no doubt can reach it, and such that it does not float up to the intellect to be debated again. It is a conviction upon which the heart is bound.

We have previously explained this matter: the senses convey sensible perceptions and propositions to the intellect, which weighs them against one another and sifts them. Whatever it becomes convinced of settles in the heart as a belief and principle that one follows and believes in, such that it does not float back to the intellect again.

This certainty has degrees: first, knowledge of certainty (ilm al-yaqin), then eye-certainty (ayn al-yaqin), then truth-certainty (haqq al-yaqin). Knowledge of certainty is when someone tells you the news and you are truthful, in whose truthfulness you have no doubt. Eye-certainty is when you see it with your own eye. Truth-certainty is when you directly experience it yourself.

I said: we once went to Indonesia and saw there a banana finger about half a meter long. When I returned I informed my children of that, so they had knowledge of it, because they trust me and know that I do not lie.

When I saw them astonished by the report, I opened the (shantah, bag) and took out banana fingers from it. When they saw them, they had eye-certainty regarding this matter, but perhaps it was something other than bananas, or a model of some other material. So we took the bananas, cut them up, and ate from them, and the matter turned into truth-certainty.

These three stages are mentioned in the Qur'an in Surat al-Takathur: ﴿No! If you knew with the certainty of knowledge, you would surely see the Hellfire. Then you will surely see it with the eye of certainty.﴾ [al-Takathur: 5-7], and in Surat al-Waqi'ah: ﴿Indeed, this is the Truth of certainty. So exalt the name of your Lord, the Most Great.﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 95-96].

Translation:

That is: among His cosmic signs that demonstrate His power, may He be exalted, is the alternation of the night and the day. In other verses we have learned that the night alone is a sign and the day alone is a sign, but the discussion here is about the alternation of the night and the day, and the mere alternation of the two is one of the signs of Allah.

The night and the day differ in several respects: they differ in the darkness of the night and the light of the day; they differ in length, being long and short; and likewise they differ in function, as they are two containers for the time of events. The night may lengthen and the day shorten, or the day may lengthen and the night shorten, and then the two become equal in duration.

For example, we find the night lengthening in winter and shortening in summer, and this is for a wisdom. We work throughout the winter day, when the weather is moderate and helps work; therefore we need a longer period of rest, and we find that in the long winter night.

Then, if you look at the night and the day in a broader view that encompasses the whole terrestrial globe, you find that they overlap: the day for you is night for others, and the night for you is day for others. So they exist together, but in distant places on the earth.

Thus you find that every moment of time in which a night begins and a day ends, or in which a day begins and a night ends. So it is a circular movement that never ends, with different timings throughout all of time.

If we take, for example, the adhan (call to prayer), we find that it circulates in every moment of time with every one of its words. At the moment you say "Allahu akbar," another says "Ashhadu alla ilaha illallah," another says "Ashhadu anna Muhammadan rasul Allah," and so on.

The same applies to the prayer. When you pray Dhuhr, another prays 'Asr, another prays Maghrib, and yet another prays 'Isha' at that very moment. So we can say that all times exist at all times, that the Truth, glorified is He, is worshipped at every moment with all kinds of worship, and that the words of the adhan echo in the hearing of the whole world, embracing all time and all place.

All of this is from the alternation of the night and the day in length and shortness, and the lengthening and shortening result from the movement of the sun. This is another matter that requires careful observation: the sun, when it rises for you, sets for others, so every east for one people is a west for others.

This explains to us His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Lord of the two easts and Lord of the two wests﴾ [Ar-Rahman: 17], where He said "two easts" and "two wests," because the east for you is the west for others at the same time.

When you look at the extension of time in its minute parts down to the second, you find easts and wests, as He, glorified is He, said: ﴿By the Lord of the easts and the wests...﴾ [Al-Ma'arij: 40]. When you look at one place, you find an east and a west, and He, glorified is He, said: ﴿The Lord of the East and the West...﴾ [Al-Muzzammil: 9]. So He is truthful in all that He has told us, glorified is He.

Among the signs of the night and the day also is that Allah made them a succession (khilfah), meaning the night succeeds the day and the day succeeds the night. He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And it is He who made the night and the day in succession for whoever wishes to remember or wishes to be grateful﴾ [Al-Furqan: 62].

From this verse we have understood that the earth is spherical. This modern scientific theory was affirmed by the Qur'an and preceded it. The meaning of the night and the day being a succession is that the earth is like a sphere, such that at the first creation the earth was created with one side facing the sun.

That side became the day, and the side opposite to it became the night. So the night and the day were created together and born together. Then when the earth rotated, the night succeeded the day and the day succeeded the night. Had the earth not been spherical, this would not have occurred.

Allah, glorified is He, emphasized this truth more clearly in His saying: ﴿It is not for the sun to overtake the moon, nor does the night outstrip the day, and each in an orbit is swimming﴾ [Ya-Sin: 40]. This is because the Arabs used to believe that the night precedes the day, so they dated their rites by the cycle of the moon. We know the day from the sun, we know the month from the moon, and from the month the year is formed.

Likewise, Ramadan is established by its night, not its day, because it depends on the appearance of the crescent. Therefore they believed that the night precedes the day, so the Qur'an corrected this belief for them, saying: ﴿nor does the night outstrip the day﴾ [Ya-Sin: 40]. It agreed with them that the day does not precede the night, and corrected for them ﴿nor does the night outstrip the day﴾ [Ya-Sin: 40].

So they were created at one time, and this cannot be unless the earth is spherical. Neither of them has precedence over the other.

As for His saying, glorified is He: ﴿And what Allah sends down from the sky of provision, and gives life thereby to the earth after its death...﴾ [Al-Jathiyah: 5]: Allah sent down from the sky many signs, some material and some immaterial. The immaterial is the Book which He sent down upon the Messenger of Allah for the guidance of creation, and the material is like the rain, which He called provision because it is the cause of provision when it descends upon the earth and gives it life with plants and fruits.

Every provision that comes from the exalted, creating side is "sent down," even if it is in the depths of the earth. Therefore He, glorified is He, said about iron: ﴿And We sent down iron, in which is great might and benefits for people...﴾ [Al-Hadid: 25]. Therefore Allah made it a means to demonstrate His power to those who oppose the religion, and He said at the end of the verse: ﴿so that Allah may know who supports Him and His messengers unseen...﴾ [Al-Hadid: 25].

His saying: ﴿from the sky...﴾ [Al-Jathiyah: 5]: it is known that the sky is not a place for water. The water is in the clouds, and, as we have said, it is a suburb of the earth and follows it. As for the sky, it is something else, too far for the mind to imagine. What is meant is: from the direction of the sky.

Whoever reflects on the cycle of water in nature finds that on the earth, where three-quarters of the terrestrial globe is water, most of it is salt water. This is for a wisdom: the proportion of salt in water protects it from change and staleness. Through evaporation clouds form, and rain falls carrying fresh water, suitable for drinking and for agriculture and other uses.

Among the signs of Allah in water is that the area of salt water expands so that the area of evaporation expands, and consequently the surface of evaporation of fresh water increases, which then suffices for the life of living beings on the earth. Then you find the saltiness of water in seas and oceans at the appropriate measure that protects water from corruption and allows the living of fish and other marine animals.

If the salinity exceeded this limit, the fish wealth would die in it, as we find, for example, in the Dead Sea, where the proportion of salinity increases because it is enclosed and no supply comes to it from other tributaries that would reduce its salinity.

To know the power of Allah in sending down sweet water from the clouds, this water which suffices for drinking and for cultivating the land, look at how much a bottle of distilled water costs when you prepare it in the laboratory. This water comes down to you from the sky sweet, clear, and pure, without effort from you and without expenses.

This water in itself is a sign of Allah's signs, because by it life exists; therefore the Qur'an called it provision. Some said: it means a cause of provision; and some said: no, rather it itself is provision. It is a cause of provision when we irrigate crops with it, but it is provision when we drink it or put it into food.

His saying: ﴿then gives life thereby to the earth after its death...﴾ [Al-Jathiyah: 5] is another sign: the dead earth is the barren, parched land where there is no plant. Allah gives it life with vegetation, as He said in another verse: ﴿And you see the earth lifeless, but when We send down upon it water, it stirs and swells...﴾ [Al-Hajj: 5].

Then he moves to another sign: ﴿and the changing of the winds...﴾ [Al-Jathiyah: 5].

The changing of the winds means: altering their direction from here to there, or altering their conditions. Sometimes it is a gentle breeze, sometimes a violent wind, sometimes hot, sometimes cold, sometimes fertilizing and sometimes destructive. These are all conditions of the winds, which their Creator, mighty and majestic is He, directs as He wills, and no one else directs them.

When you examine and reflect on the process of the changing of the winds, you find in it a manifestation of the miracle of the Creator, glorified is He. Look at these towers and skyscrapers, and ask yourself: who erects these giant buildings? And who supports them so that they do not lean despite the storms blowing upon them?

What supports them is the air that surrounds them from every side. If you emptied one side of them of air, they would collapse on that empty side of air.

So the air is what preserves their balance. Therefore, whenever you find the Qur'an using the word "al-riyah" (the winds) in the plural, know that it is for prosperity and good, and when it is singular, it is for destruction and ruin.

A single wind destroys, while the winds support and build, because this one comes from one direction, and that one comes from all directions, thus producing the required balance.

And read here, in the context of speaking about the signs of Allah and enumerating His blessings: ﴿and the changing of the winds...﴾ [Al-Jathiyah: 5]. In another verse He, glorified is He, said: ﴿Rather, it is what you sought to hasten: a wind in which is a painful punishment, destroying everything by the command of its Lord...﴾ [Al-Ahqaf: 24–25]. And He said: ﴿And in 'Ad, when We sent upon them the barren wind, which left nothing it passed over but that it made it like decayed remains﴾ [Adh-Dhariyat: 41–42].

His saying: ﴿Indeed in that are signs for a people who reason﴾ [Al-Jathiyah: 5], because reason is what receives events, discusses them, distinguishes between matters, extracts truth from them, and delivers it to the heart, where it becomes a firm belief that does not accept doubt.

May Allah have mercy on Fakhr al-Din al-Razi, who made a precise scientific comparison between these verses in al-Jathiyah, beginning with His saying: ﴿Indeed, in the heavens and the earth are signs for the believers﴾ [Al-Jathiyah: 3] up to ﴿for a people who reason﴾ [Al-Jathiyah: 5], and between verse 164 of Surat al-Baqarah: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of the night and the day and the ships which sail through the sea with that which benefits people, and what Allah sends down from the sky of rain, giving life thereby to the earth after its death and dispersing therein every creature, and the changing of the winds and the clouds controlled between the sky and the earth are signs for a people who reason﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 164].

First: he found the first difference between the two passages is that al-Jathiyah has ﴿Indeed, in the heavens and the earth...﴾ [Al-Jathiyah: 3], whereas al-Baqarah has ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth...﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 164]. Both have the same meaning, because khalq (creation) is the act of bringing into existence, and the act itself is called khalq, and it is also applied to the created thing, as evidenced by His saying: ﴿This is the creation of Allah﴾ [Luqman: 11], meaning His creation.

So the meaning in both passages is one.

Second: he counted the cosmic signs mentioned in al-Jathiyah and found them to be six, while in al-Baqarah there are eight. When he investigated the addition in al-Baqarah, he found it in His saying: ﴿and the ships which sail through the sea with that which benefits people...﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 164] and ﴿and the clouds controlled between the sky and the earth...﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 164].

He said: these two signs, the ships and the clouds, are dispensed with by His saying in al-Jathiyah, ﴿and the changing of the winds﴾ [Al-Jathiyah: 5], because they move by the movement of the winds.

The last difference between the two passages is that the verse of al-Baqarah ends with one phrase, ﴿for a people who reason﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 164], whereas the verses of al-Jathiyah contain three phrases: ﴿for the believers﴾ [Al-Jathiyah: 3], ﴿for a people who have certainty﴾ [Al-Jathiyah: 4], and ﴿for a people who reason﴾ [Al-Jathiyah: 5].

The believer, when he hears from Allah, affirms and believes what Allah has informed; and certainty belongs to the seeker of truth who searches for it in a scientific matter and wishes to reach certainty through it.

A person who is neither a firm believer nor a seeker of truth still has at least some measure of reason by which he distinguishes between things, and knows by it what to eat, what to drink, what to take, and what to leave.

So these three phrases represent the stages of sound perception. Reasoning is the lowest rank, and for this reason the verse of al-Baqarah ended with it.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 45, verse 6:

﴿These﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 6] is a reference to the verses of the Qur'an, or to the cosmic signs that preceded it. ﴿We recite them to you in truth﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 6]. Truth, as we have said, is that which is firm and does not change, and its opposite is falsehood (batil). Truth is the judgment of a proposition that corresponds to reality, and falsehood is the judgment of a proposition that contradicts reality.

For this reason we have said: the witness of truth does not change his statements no matter how often you repeat the question to him, whereas the witness of false testimony must alter his statements, because the witness of truth depicts a reality, so it comes out one and unchanging, while the witness of falsehood depicts illusions and imaginings, so they must change.

For this reason, God, glory be to Him, wants us to hold to the truth and make it the measure of all things, just as we take the metre, for example, as a unit of measurement and do not depart from it.

He wants us to judge by the truth and to make it the foundation in building things. The clock cannot keep correct time for you unless it is itself precisely regulated.

For this reason God, exalted is He, said concerning the sun and the moon: ﴿The sun and the moon [run] by a reckoning﴾ [al-Rahman: 5], meaning: they were created with precise calculation. And because they were created with reckoning, God made them an instrument for measuring time. Whatever you take as a measure, you must first measure it by the truth and establish it upon the truth.

For this reason He, glory be to Him, informed us that He created the heavens and the earth in truth, and they proceed by a precise and firm balance that never fails, from the time God created this universe until the Hour arrives.

We have said that because truth is that which is firm and unchanging, it is what remains, it is what is victorious, and it is what prevails at the end of the struggle. If falsehood rises high, that is only for a time, and He gives falsehood a chance so that people may be bitten by it and society may suffer from it, and then people return to the arena of truth.

For this reason we say: falsehood is a soldier from the soldiers of truth. If Islam rose in the Arabian Peninsula through the inimitability of the Qur'an, how did it rise and spread into the lands of Persia and Rome?

It is said: because at that time they were subdued by falsehood, and when they saw the justice and tolerance of Islam they hastened to it. For this reason Islam conquered half the world within half a century, because people were longing for such a true religion.

God, exalted is He, wants to give us a tangible image that depicts truth and falsehood in a single picture, so He says, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿He sends down water from the sky, and the valleys flow according to their measure, and the torrent carries a swelling foam. And from what they heat in the fire, seeking ornament or goods, there is a foam like it. Thus God strikes [the parable of] truth and falsehood. As for the foam, it passes away as scum, but as for that which benefits people, it remains upon the earth. Thus God sets forth the parables﴾ [al-Ra'd: 17].

As for His saying, glory be to Him: ﴿In what statement after God and His signs will they believe?﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 6], meaning: if all these cosmic signs and all this inimitability do not persuade them, and if the speech of God does not persuade them, then by what will they believe after that? So the matter, as far as they are concerned, is obstinacy and stubborn perversity. If the word of God does not persuade them, what word after it will persuade them?

We ask them: is there a statement more truthful than the statement of God? Or an report more truthful than His report? He, glory be to Him, makes Himself agreeable to you by explaining His signs in His creation so that you may believe, and so that He may take you by the hand to the arena of faith, while He is without need of you. He only cares for you because you are His servants and His handiwork, and He wants you in the best condition.

For this reason He sent you messengers, revealed to you books, and made clear to you the lawful and the unlawful, and truth and falsehood. Why then this stubbornness? And why this obstinacy regarding faith?

Yet belief in God is an honour, and servitude to Him is might. The word "servitude" (ʿubudiyyah) is a hated word that indicates humiliation and submission, but with God it is honour, dignity and might.

The word "Wayl" (woe, ruin): they said it is a valley in Hell, or a destruction from which there is no escape or deliverance. The word "wayl" differs according to the one who utters it and threatens with it. When someone like you says to you, "Woe to you," you expect the woe to be commensurate with his power over you and his ability to carry out what he threatened you with of his assault and destruction.

If the One who speaks this threat is Allah, glorified is He, we understand that it is an inevitable ruin that no one can withstand, a great woe that cannot be repelled or averted.

So for whom is this threat? ﴿Woe to every sinful liar.﴾ The "affak" (sinful liar) is from "ifk," which is turning a thing over from its proper face, or deliberately turning realities upside down. Among its uses is the words of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿And the overturned cities He hurled down﴾ [al-Najm: 53], which are the towns that Allah, exalted is He, overturned upside down, making their upper part their lower part.

Among its uses also is the story of the slander against Lady 'Aisha: ﴿Indeed, those who came with the slander are a group among you...﴾ [al-Nur: 11]. Therefore, "ifk" is the most grievous kind of lying, because it is deliberate lying that turns people away from the truth toward falsehood.

It does not harm just one person; its harm falls upon a multitude of people. Its evil extends outward, so it incurs a punishment proportionate to this extension over creation. Therefore, whenever you hear the word "wayl," know that it is for a great sin.

As for the word "affak," it is an intensive form on the pattern of "fa''al." Had he lied only once, he would be called "afik," but this sin was repeated from him until he exceeded in it. Similarly in intensiveness is "athim," meaning one who commits much sin. It is also an intensive form on the pattern of "fa'il," i.e., one who exceeds in sins.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 45, verse 8:

The word (ويل) (wayl). They said: it is a valley in Hell, or a destruction from which there is no escape and no deliverance. The word wayl varies according to the one who utters it and the threat he gives. When someone like you says to you: "Wayl to you!", you expect the wayl to be in proportion to his power over you and his ability to carry out the threat of his violence and destruction.

If the one who speaks this threat is Allah, glorified is He, we understand that it is an inevitable destruction, that no one can withstand, a great wayl that cannot be turned back or repelled.

So, to whom is this threat directed? ﴿Woe to every sinful liar﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 7]. The afik (أفَّاك) comes from ifk (إفك), which is turning a thing upside down or deliberately reversing the facts. Among its uses is the words of the Exalted: ﴿And the overturned cities He hurled down﴾ [al-Najm: 53], which are the towns that Allah, exalted is He, turned upside down, making their highest part their lowest.

Also among its uses is the story of the slander against Lady 'Aishah: ﴿Indeed, those who came with the slander are a group among you...﴾ [al-Nur: 11]. Therefore, ifk is the most heinous kind of lying, because it is deliberate lying that turns people away from the truth towards falsehood.

It does not harm one person only; its harm falls on a multitude of people. Its evil extends and it entails a punishment proportionate to this extension over creation. Therefore, whenever you hear the word (ويل) (wayl), know that it is for a great sin.

The word ﴿afik﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 7] is an intensive form (sigha mubalaghah) on the pattern fa''al (فعَّال). If he had lied only once, he would be (آفِك) (afik, a liar). This sin was repeated by him until he exaggerated in it. Similar in intensification is ﴿athim﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 7], meaning: one who commits much sin. It is also an intensive form, on the pattern fa'il (فعيل), i.e., one who exaggerates in sins. You say: athim (آثم) and athim (أثيم), like: 'alim (عالم) and 'alim (عليم).

If a person understands one of the sciences, he is called 'alim (عالم). But 'alim (عليم) means knowledge in its essence. Therefore it is not said except of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And over every possessor of knowledge is one [more] Knowing﴾ [Yusuf: 76]. It is as if this sinner has become so practised in sin that it has become his nature and his habit.

Then the Exalted describes this sinful liar, saying: ﴿He hears the verses of Allah recited to him, then persists arrogantly as if he had not heard them...﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 8]. It is as if the Exalted wishes to make us know falsehood in its true nature. The liar lies to someone like himself, or lies to a family or a group, but this one lies to the whole world when he distorts the facts and reverses them, deliberately.

This is the meaning of ﴿persists arrogantly...﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 8]. For this reason, in law they say "with premeditation and lying in wait" (سَبْق الإصرار والترصُّد). ﴿Arrogantly (مُستكبراً)﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 8] means: exalting himself above the truth.

In the noble hadith: "Arrogance is rejecting the truth and looking down on people." He is arrogant because the verses come to him through someone whom he believes to be beneath him. Thus he has wronged the truth and wronged one who holds the truth, as the Qur'an relates about them: ﴿And they said: "Why was this Qur'an not sent down upon a man of great standing from one of the two cities?"﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 31].

So the problem for them is not with the Qur'an, for they are people of eloquence and rhetoric who know the inimitability of the Qur'an and its truthfulness. Rather, they envy the man through whose hands the Qur'an came, measuring him by their standards of status and wealth.

In their view, the message should come through a rich man, one of the great men of the people and of the nobility. This is strange of them, because the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had a great standing among them before the Prophethood, and they used to speak of his truthfulness and trustworthiness. This is evident from their making him the judge in the matter of the Black Stone when they wanted to place it in its position and disagreed about it. The contradiction in their positions towards him is clear: they would say he was a sorcerer, a soothsayer, a liar, and a poet. Then, when the revelation paused, they said: "The Lord of Muhammad has forsaken him."

As for the Exalted's words: ﴿So give them good tidings of a painful punishment﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 8]. It is well known that bushrah (بشارة) is the announcement of good before its time. He called it bushrah because it shows joy and happiness on the faces at the moment you hear news that pleases you. The use of bushrah for punishment is by way of mockery and derision, and it is a form of punishment and humiliation. Like a man who kept urging his son to study and strive, but the son disobeyed his father's orders. When the result appeared and he found his son had failed, he said to him: "Good news, you have failed!" He intends to mock him and punish him for his negligence.

Because, after he has persisted in turning away from God's signs, and after he has grown arrogant toward them, he must at some moment return to himself and put his mind to what he hears, so that some knowledge of God's signs reaches him. ﴿And when he knows anything of Our signs, he takes it in mockery..﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 9] He makes it a subject of ridicule and derision. ﴿For them is a humiliating punishment﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 9]. And before that, the Lord of Might gave him the good news that he has a painful punishment.

These are different kinds of punishment, we seek refuge in God. The painful punishment is that which pains the senses and hurts, and the body and the limbs are affected by it. This is other than the humiliating punishment. The aspects, as they say, are distinct. The humiliating punishment is the punishment of the soul, in which it is debased and humiliated and its dignity is destroyed, because some people are not pained by a physical blow, but are pained that their dignity is wounded, even by a single word.

In other verses there is also (a great punishment), meaning: exaggerated. Thus the Exalted has gathered upon them every kind of punishment, as recompense for their arrogance, obstinacy and defiance regarding the signs of God, and these are too clear for any denier to deny.

Here He used the verbal noun ﴿huzuwan﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 9] to indicate exaggeration, and that mockery has become a necessary attribute of his, clinging to him, as we say: "So-and-so is just," and "So-and-so is justice," as if you made him and justice one thing.

The verse also shows that when a person devotes himself to the truth, empties his mind, and then thinks with his intellect about things objectively, he must reach the thread that leads him to the truth. Sincere return to oneself leads to the truth.

Therefore, the Exalted teaches people how to think soundly and how to seek the truth, saying: ﴿Say: I admonish you with one thing: that you stand up for God, in pairs and singly, then reflect: there is no madness in your companion﴾ [Saba': 46]. That is: abandon the thinking of the masses and their partisanship, for it is disorderly and leads to chaos in which the truth gets lost.

Thought is the work of the intellect, and the intellect is the authority that protects you from misguided opinions, guides you, and takes you by the hand to the truth. Even in its name, the intellect (ʿaql) derives from the ʿiqal, the tether that restrains the animal from straying from its owner; likewise the intellect restrains its possessor (ya'qilu sahibahu).

So: these people, when they returned to themselves and used their minds, were restrained and reached some of the truth, but their pride and obstinacy prevented them from following it. The clearest proof of this is the saying of some of them to others: ﴿Do not listen to this Qur'an, and make noise during it, that perhaps you may prevail﴾ [Fussilat: 26].

Had they not been certain of the truthfulness of the Qur'an and of its effect on souls, they would not have said this. But the style of the Qur'an captivated them and penetrated into their depths. Had they left themselves in their natural disposition, they would have believed; but they received the Qur'an with souls filled with impulses of evil and love of escape from the bonds of the true method that this Qur'an brought.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 45, verse 10:

The word (wara') in the language (lughah) has several meanings, the clearest of which is in His words ﴿So they threw it behind their backs..﴾ [Aal Imran: 187], meaning: behind their backs. And this is the well-known meaning of the word wara'?

But it also comes with the meaning of that which will come to you in the future, as in this verse ﴿Before them is Hell..﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 10], for it awaits them in the future.

And (wara') comes with the meaning of "in front of," as in His words, may He be exalted, in the verse of al-Kahf: ﴿And there was behind them a king who seized every ship by force﴾ [al-Kahf: 79]. The events of the story say that the king was waiting for them on the shore to seize every sound ship, so he was in front of them, not behind them.

The wara' is that which has, beyond it, something that conceals it. What conceals knowledge is either the veil of time or the veil of place. So we, for example, are now sitting in one place, and each of us sees the other, but we do not see whoever is outside this place. What conceals him from us, then, is the veil of place.

When I tell you about the future, you find the future time also hidden from you by the veil of the future time. Likewise, in the past time, the veil of the past time has hidden it from you.

The knowledge of the Real, glorified is He, pierces all these veils, and time with Him is the same, whether past, present or future. Therefore He brings up the past and speaks of it as if it were present, and He, glorified is He, says addressing His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿And you were not with them when they cast their pens, [to see] which of them would be responsible for Mary, nor were you with them when they disputed﴾ [Aal Imran: 44].

Therefore He pierces the veil of the future time, as in His words, glorified is He, concerning the struggle between Persia and Rome: ﴿Alif, Lam, Meem. The Romans have been defeated, in the nearest land, but they, after their defeat, will overcome, within a few years﴾ [al-Rum: 1-4], because the Muslims grieved over the victory of Persia over Rome.

The Persians were Magians, having no connection with revelation (al-sama'), whereas the Romans were People of the Book, who believe in the messengers. The lot of Islam was that the Romans would be victorious, so God gave them good news of that victory before it happened by a few years, and the bid' (a few) in the language is from three to nine years.

So the Real informs His Prophet of future events in a Qur'an that is recited and worshipped with in every prayer. How then would the Messenger announce this good news, and the people in Persia and in Rome hear it? Therefore, he announces it while certain that it is truth and sincerity, and that it must come to pass.

This is a piercing of the veil of the future. Indeed, after a few years the Romans defeated Persia, and that coincided with the victory of the Muslims over the disbelievers at Badr. So He, glorified is He, said: ﴿And on that day the believers will rejoice * in the victory of God..﴾ [al-Rum: 4-5].

So His words, glorified is He: ﴿Before them is Hell..﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 10], meaning: it awaits them in the future. It is in front of them, and this is a piercing of the veil of the future time.

﴿Nor will what they earned avail them at all..﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 10], meaning: it will not repel from them the evil of what they are in, because of what they acquired in the past of worshipping idols and deifying God's creation. And does an idol avail its worshipper, when it was he who made it? And when the wind overturns it and knocks it down, does he set it up again? Likewise, those among humans whom they worshipped will precede them into Hell. So there is no helper for them and no one to defend them.

He used this bare verb (kasaba) for evil, and did not say iktasabu. We have previously explained that kasaba is used for good and iktasaba for evil, because good and obedience come naturally with no contrivance in them, unlike disobedience, which requires contrivance and scheming.

And kasaba is not used for evil except when evil has become a habit and has taken on, for its owner, the status of acquisition (kasb), so that he no longer shrinks from it, and it has become easy for him to fall into it time after time until evil has become his custom.

So He said: ﴿what they earned..﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 10], that is, of evil, ﴿nor what they took as protectors besides God﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 10], that is, the gods they worshipped besides God. Likewise, they do not avail them, ﴿and for them is a great punishment﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 10]. So the matter does not end at their being forsaken and not being defended, but for them there is also a great punishment, meaning: severe and exceeding in causing pain.

This is a demonstrative referring to the guidance, which is the method that our master, the Messenger of God (ﷺ), brought in this Qur'an. Guidance (al-hudā) is that which guides you, meaning it points you to the path that leads to the goal by the nearest and easiest routes and the safest, without hardship to the self.

In the opening of Surat al-Baqara: ﴿They are upon guidance from their Lord﴾ [al-Baqara: 5]. So guidance is like a vehicle that carries you to your goal, and a mount that travels with you until it brings you safely through.

As for ﴿And those who disbelieved in the signs of their Lord﴾, He said "their Lord" even though they disbelieve in Him, because He, exalted is He, is a Lord who shows affection to them even in their disbelief and denial. This is, as we have said, the bestowal of lordship, which does not distinguish between believer and disbeliever: He gives to all and shows tenderness to everyone, for they are all His servants and His creation.

﴿For them is a painful punishment of a rijz [wretched affliction]﴾. Sometimes He says "a painful punishment," and sometimes "for them is a painful punishment of a rijz." Al-rijz (a severe, abasing affliction) is the most intense kind of punishment, and punishment ('adhāb) is the infliction of pain upon a living being...

The meaning of ﴿disbelieved in the signs of their Lord﴾ is: they concealed them and denied them. So the signs exist, but they hid them. Similarly, "disbelieved in God" means they concealed His existence, subhānahu. Concealment can only apply to something that first exists and is then covered up. Thus faith exists and its root is in the self, then disbelief comes and covers it.

Taskhir (subjugation) means taskhil (making something submissive) and that the one subjugated becomes a pledged servant to the one for whose service it is subjugated... And taskhir is imposing a thing upon something by compulsion, so that it is in the service of the vicegerent (khalifah), who is man; thus the whole universe is subjugated to him. That is: it obeys him and follows his command... And His saying: ﴿and that perhaps you may be grateful﴾ is a command to give thanks for the blessing. So whenever you see a manifestation of God's blessing, say: "All praise is due to God," and acknowledge God's favour. For this reason our master, the Messenger of God (ﷺ), taught us the supplication for boarding ships or other conveyances, and among this supplication is: "Glory be to Him who has subjected this to us, and we were not capable of it, and to our Lord indeed we are returning."

Al-Haqq, glory be to Him, moves us from the subjection of the sea to the subjection of the heavens and the earth. They have been made subservient to man since God created them, but man has not known the aspects of this subjection all at once; he comes to know them over the passage of time and the development of the sciences.

As He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿We shall show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves, until it becomes clear to them that it is the Truth..﴾ [Fussilat: 53].

For example, when you read His saying concerning the ships, ﴿And His are the ships raised high in the sea like mountains﴾ [al-Rahman: 24], you must use your reason and ask as we asked: when did people come to know ships with decks? The word al-Munshaat (the raised ones) indicates construction, and "like the mountains" means high and lofty like the mountains. They said: man came to know ships with decks at the end of the eighteenth century, and before that they were merely a flat surface with nothing on it.

So who informed the Messenger of God that ships would have raised structures like mountains? Likewise in His saying: ﴿And were it not that mankind would be one community, We would have made for those who disbelieve in the Most Merciful silver roofs for their houses and stairways [of silver] by which they ascend﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 33].

Al-Ma'arij is the plural of mi'raj, and in today's language it is (the elevator). Modern civilisation did not know the elevator until the end of the twentieth century. So these are manifestations of the miraculous nature of the Qur'an and of the truthfulness of the one who conveyed it. God has spoken truly, and His Messenger has spoken truly.

This indicates that these innovations exist in His knowledge, glory be to Him, and have their (model) before human thought reaches them, and God shows them to His servants according to their need and over the passage of time and the development of the sciences. This is the meaning of ﴿We shall show them..﴾ [Fussilat: 53].

As for His saying: ﴿And He has subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth..﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 13]. We have said that each of the heavens and the earth is a container for many things, some of which we know and some of which we have not yet reached. We look at the sky from below, and among God's creatures in it we see only the sun, the moon, the stars and the clouds, and all of this is in the lowest heaven.

Therefore He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And We have adorned the nearest heaven with lamps..﴾ [Fussilat: 12]. As for the seven heavens, that is something else, of which we know nothing. It is enough for you to know that between you and the sun there are eight light-minutes, and there are creatures between you and which is a hundred light-years; multiply that by 365 days, by 24 hours, by 60 minutes, by the speed of light.

So above you is another world beyond what your mind can imagine. Therefore He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And the heaven We constructed with strength (bi-aydin), and indeed We are expanding it﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 47]. Bi-aydin means with power.

In reflecting on the subjection of the cosmos for you, it is enough that you look at the sun, and how the Creator has subjected it for you, giving you light, warmth, energy and various rays without your expending anything in that cause, without maintenance, without fuel, and without even reaching it at all.

It works in your service since God created it until the Hour is established, requiring nothing from you. You need only benefit from it, reflect on its nature and how to exploit it for what benefits you. Likewise the moon gives you soft, calm light, and by it we are guided in the darkness of the night: ﴿And landmarks; and by the star they are guided﴾ [al-Nahl: 16].

God created the sun and the moon in the form of motion; they have been moving since God created them until the Hour is established, moving without fuel and without energy, by the law of inertia as we have said, namely that a moving body continues to move unless you halt it, and a still body remains still unless you move it. We have said that this motion is by precise and exact reckoning: ﴿The sun and the moon [move] by precise calculation﴾ [al-Rahman: 5].

The earth likewise is a container for many things and multiple kinds. In it is the inanimate, the lowest of the kinds; when growth is added to it, it becomes plant; when sensation is added to it, it becomes animal; when reason is added to it, it becomes man, the highest of these kinds and the most honoured by God.

Therefore God subjected all these kinds to him and placed them at his service, and made him master over them and His vicegerent on His earth.

When the Exalted spoke of the inanimate, He said: ﴿Have you not seen that God sends down water from the sky, and We produce thereby fruits of varying colours? And among the mountains are white and red streaks of varying shades, and [others] very black﴾ [Fatir: 27]. He placed fruits, which are of plants, before the inanimate, because we do not eat the inanimate; we eat plants, and fruits are their outcome and what concerns me of them, and they are among the essentials of life.

Then He spoke of the mountains, which are the source of goods, wealth, minerals and precious stones; therefore He said of them in another verse: ﴿And He placed firmly set mountains upon it from above it, and blessed it, and measured therein its sustenance..﴾ [Fussilat: 10], that is, in the mountains.

We have previously explained that the mountains are the sources and storehouses of sustenance in the earth, because they are the source of the rich, fertile soil that flows with the rainwater and spreads throughout the land, increasing its fertility: ﴿And there is not a thing but that with Us are its depositories, and We do not send it down except in a known measure﴾ [al-Hijr: 21].

Thus all kinds of creation contain signs. Consider the inanimate: look, for example, at the mountains and the varied wonders and colours in them, including marble, granite, alabaster and others. And the plant, which represents the primary source of sustenance: look, for example, at the Arab palm tree and compare it with the European palm tree. The palm among us is a source of food, and one benefits from everything in it, so that nothing of it is ever thrown away.

Therefore you will find for it a staircase that enables you to climb it to trim its fronds or gather its fruit, whereas the European palm is for ornament, and therefore you will find it smooth, difficult to climb. This is from the wisdom and precision of creation, so blessed be God, the best of creators.

Consider the palm frond: you will find it broad at its base and slender and thin at its tip. The leaves on it are the opposite: flat and spread out on the upper side, then they curve until they become thorns at the base of the frond, near the fruit. This is because these thorns protect the fruit from rats. Then consider that these thorns end at the base of the frond and do not extend to the strands that bear the fruit.

Then consider the trunk: in the palm it is long and straight, unlike other trees, which are short and branching, because their fruits are small and easy to carry on branches. As for the watermelon, for example, its fruit is on a thin, spiralling stem that spreads along the ground, because the fruit is heavy.

So the matter is power, not mechanics. In eating, for example, you eat the peel of the apricot and leave the kernel, whereas with the almond you eat the kernel and leave the shell. This is the boundless power and high wisdom of the Creator, mighty and majestic. You eat the fig entirely, as it has no peel, whereas the orange or the tangerine has a peel. Then consider the variety of colours and flavours in plants, though they are watered with one water. And say: glory be to the Creator.

Consider trees: you will find some green trees with no fruit, and you think they have no use. But they must have a use, either for you or for other creatures. It suffices that they are an adornment and beauty and a source of oxygen, and perhaps they have benefits you do not know. For example, you will find some of these trees have flowers of different shapes, colours and scents.

This is another world of aesthetic creativity in nature. These varied colours and scents have wisdom, because they attract butterflies and insects that carry out the pollination of crops, and each butterfly or insect has its own disposition in colour and scent.

Therefore, when insecticides spread, this phenomenon diminished, and we no longer see flowers in the fields. Why? Because the insecticides killed the butterflies that carry out the task of pollination.

When you reflect on the process of pollination itself, you find in it a sign of creation and of God's wondrous workmanship, the Exalted. Among crops there are some whose pollination we know how it occurs, such as the palm, and we know that there is a male and a female, and this is clear in the shape of the tree. But the mango tree, for example, how does pollination occur in it? We do not know.

When you see all this beauty in creation, you must remember the Creator and say: blessed be God, the best of creators. And more beautiful than beauty is He who created beauty.

The phrase ﴿all of it from Him..﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 13]: the word "jami'an" (all of it) is one of the words of emphasis. It means that everything in the heavens and everything on the earth is from God without exception, so every small thing and every great thing, from the atom to the galaxy, is by God's bounty, whether you know it or whether your knowledge has not encompassed it.

The word (minhu, "from Him") was read by some as (minnatan, "as a favour"), and the meaning does not deviate from the intended one: it is from God, and it is a favour from God.

You know that when the Qur'an was first collected, it was collected without dots and without vowel marks, relying on the Arab linguistic faculty to grasp and derive its meanings. It is related that Hammad al-Rawiya did not have the Qur'an memorised, and when they brought him the codex he read: ﴿My punishment, I afflict with it whom I will..﴾ [al-A'raf: 156], with the sin (as-sin, "with s") which keeps the meaning correct, but the word of the Qur'an is (ashaa').

And he read: "the craftsmanship of God, and who is better in craftsmanship than God" (sun'at Allah), pronouncing the ghayn as ayn, and it is the same meaning.

Thus the gift of the Qur'an is an enduring gift, and one who has a taste for Arabic can reach its meanings and wisdom. But when the linguistic faculties declined, they were compelled to add dots and vowel marks so that the meaning might be clear, although in earlier times they considered marking the book to be an ill opinion of the one to whom it was addressed, because it implied an accusation that he could not understand it.

Then He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Indeed in that..﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 13], that is, in these subjected creatures, ﴿are signs..﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 13], wonders and proofs, ﴿for a people who reflect﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 13].

So this is a call to faith. The Exalted presents to us His workmanship and His creativity in the universe, and calls us to reflect upon it and to employ our minds in it, and a craftsman does not display his craft in this way unless he is confident of its quality.

We have said: if you go to a cloth seller to buy, for example, a woollen suit, he displays the cloth to you and shows you its quality; then he takes a thread from it and sets fire to it before you to show you the reality of that quality. He does not do this unless he is confident in his goods.

But the other, the seller of spoilt, adulterated goods, deceives you, lies to you with words, trickery and falsehood, and dares not show you the reality of what he has.

So when your Lord addresses you: "Use your reason, reflect, remember," this means that if you apply thought to this verse, it would lead you to the Truth and to His purpose for you. Therefore the Truth warns His servants against turning away from the signs: ﴿And how many a sign in the heavens and the earth they pass by, while they turn away from it﴾ [Yusuf: 105].

Then al-Haqq, glory be to Him, says:

﴿Say to those who believe: forgive those who do not expect the days of...﴾.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 45, verse 14:

The word (qul, "say") shows the scrupulous accuracy of the Messenger of Allah in conveying from Allah, and that he (ﷺ) does not bring anything from himself, nor does he convey the speech of Allah by its meaning but by its letters. Otherwise, in the words of the Exalted, ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾ [al-Ikhlas: 1], he could have said to the people: "Allah is One."

Take, for example, when you send your son to his uncle and say to him: "Say to your uncle: My father wants you." The boy goes and says to his uncle: "My father wants you." The meaning has been conveyed with this wording, and the expression has been completed without "say."

As for the Messenger of Allah, he utters what Allah uttered, and does not interfere with the text of what was revealed to him, as if he is saying to us: "This speech is not from me; it is the speech of Allah, which he conveys just as he heard it."

It is strange that we hear someone calling for the deletion of this word from the Mushaf, claiming that it adds nothing to the meaning. We say to him: It is enough that Allah uttered it and His Messenger (ﷺ) uttered it. Moreover, it has a function, as we have explained.

﴿Say to those who believe: Let them forgive those who do not hope for the Days of Allah...﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 14], that is: let them pardon and overlook, and not take them to account for trivialities, so long as these do not go beyond speech to action.

﴿Those who do not hope for the Days of Allah...﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 14], that is: those who do not fear the Days of Allah, nor take warning from them, nor reckon with them. Hope (raja') is a kind of seeking, and it contains a sense of wishing and of desire for the attainment of what one hopes for. Hope is the seeking of a thing that is expected to occur.

Wishing (tamanni) is the opposite of this, being the seeking of what is impossible and far out of reach, as the poet said:

"Would that youth might return one day, so that I might tell it what old age has done."

As for hope, it is the expectation that it may come to pass. You say: "I hope to be granted success" or "I hope to travel."

The meaning of ﴿the Days of Allah...﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 14], as when we say, for example, "the days of the Arabs," means their battles and the great events that passed over them. So the Days of Allah means His encounters with His enemies: the Days of Allah for the believers are His victory for them, and for the disbelievers their defeat. They do not pause at these events, nor reflect upon them, nor take a lesson from them, but pass over them like the noble who passes by, or like the heedless who is unaware of the judgment of things. These are the hypocrites.

This verse has a story. During the expedition of Banu al-Mustaliq there was a well from which they drank, called al-Muraysi'. At this well gathered a servant of Umar ibn al-Khattab and a servant of Abdullah ibn Ubayy, the chief of the hypocrites. Umar's servant prevented the other, saying: "No, not until I have watered the Messenger of Allah first." The other said: "Have you finished?" He said: "No, the bucket of Abu Bakr is still to come, then the bucket of Umar." He said: "This is because he knows that he is a hypocrite."

The servant was late in returning to Abdullah ibn Ubayy, who said: "What delayed you?" He said: "A client of Umar ibn al-Khattab did such and such." Ibn Ubayy shook his head in the manner of a hypocrite and said: "We and they are as the speaker said: Fatten your dog and it will eat you." He said this word to relieve what was in his breast. This word reached Umar, who took his sword and wanted to kill him, but Allah revealed this verse: ﴿Say to those who believe: Let them forgive those who do not hope for the Days of Allah...﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 14].

Yes, they should forgive them and overlook these slips, because they are within the realm of speech and have not reached the level of deeds. When they reach action, they have a different status, as happened in the matter of the Muslim woman of Banu Qaynuqa', when one of them lifted the hem of her garment upward, and when she stood up her private part was exposed, so there had to be a speech that would discipline them.

As for speech, there is no harm in tolerating it from these hypocrites. And it is enough against the hypocrite that he humiliates himself by his hypocrisy, because he does what he does not believe in and does not hold to. Moreover, hypocrisy in itself is evidence of the strength of faith, since faith has become a power that is feigned, and this is from the might of faith and the abasement of hypocrisy.

For this reason the Qur'an recounted their saying: ﴿If we return to Madinah, the mightier will surely expel the meaner from it...﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 8]. So Allah confirmed their saying that the mightier should expel the meaner, but who is the mightier and who is the meaner? He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And might belongs to Allah, and to His Messenger, and to the believers...﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 8].

It is enough that these hypocrites used to stand in the first row in prayer in order to conceal their hypocrisy; within them there was contradiction and wavering, and this is a humiliation before themselves first.

It is narrated that Finhas the Jew, when the verse ﴿Who is it that will lend to Allah a goodly loan...﴾ [al-Baqarah: 245] was revealed, laughed and said: "The Lord of Muhammad has become poor, and He asks us for a loan." It was a word with which he relieved what was in his breast of rancour. Yet they were, in every battle and in every prayer, in the first row.

When the Exalted and Most High commanded the believers to forgive these hypocrites, it was only so that the hypocrite would be humbled before himself. For this reason the orientalists raised an uproar over His saying: ﴿When the hypocrites come to you, they say: We bear witness that you are indeed the Messenger of Allah; and Allah knows that you are indeed His Messenger...﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 1], and how He then says: ﴿And Allah bears witness that the hypocrites are indeed liars﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 1].
