That is because there is a difference between the saying and what is said. They are truthful in what is said, which is ﴿that you are indeed the Messenger of Allah...﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 1], but they are liars in the saying, because they are hypocrites.

So the Exalted did not call them liars regarding "you are indeed the Messenger of Allah." Rather, He called them liars in their saying ﴿We bear witness...﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 1], because testimony means the agreement of the heart with the tongue, and the hypocrite's heart is in one valley while his tongue is in another.

Therefore: the meaning of ﴿the Days of Allah...﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 14] is the well-known events, such as the day of Badr, Uhud and al-Hudaybiyah. These days contain victory for the Muslims that gladdens them and soothes their hearts, and defeat for the disbelievers that grieves them and troubles their lives. Likewise are the events that befell the nations that denied the messengers.

These hypocrites do not fear these events, in the sense that they do not take warning from them. Therefore they were not turned away from obstinacy, contention and stubbornness. This matter is explained by the Exalted in His saying: ﴿So each We seized for his sin: among them were those upon whom We sent a storm of stones, and among them were those seized by the Cry, and among them were those whom We caused the earth to swallow, and among them were those We drowned...﴾ [al-Ankabut: 40].

And His saying, glory be to Him: ﴿That He may recompense a people for what they used to earn﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 14]. It is as if the Exalted says to His Prophet: "Leave them to Me." Therefore, the command to forgive these people is not an honouring of them nor a mercy towards them, but so that a greater and more severe punishment may befall them, and so that the Exalted may Himself take them to task by His power, glory be to Him.

Therefore: clear the ground for them to the vengeance of Allah upon them, for in reality they do not stand against you, but against the Exalted.

Furthermore, forgiveness has its foundations and its limits. You forgive the one who does evil, and you forgive and forgive, and in return you find nothing but obstinacy and denial. At that point you must shift from forbearance to ignorance (in the sense of refusing to be imposed upon), which is more beneficial and more fitting in that situation.

The Arab poet perceived this meaning and said:

"Part of forbearance is to employ ignorance in place of it, when the paths of wrongdoing have widened in the face of forbearance."

Another said:

"We pardoned the Banu Dhuhl, and we said: the people are brothers.
Perhaps the days will return them to what they were."

"But when evil became manifest and grew naked,
we walked the walk of the lion going forth, while the lion was angry,
with a blow that brings weakness, debility and subjugation,
and a thrust like the mouth of a waterskin going forth while the waterskin is full.
And some forbearance in the face of ignorance is submission to humiliation,
and in evil there is salvation when kindness will not save you."

As for the saying of the Exalted ﴿for what they used to earn﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 14], it was previously explained that kasaba is said of good, and iktasaba of evil, because the form with the infix carries the sense of effort. Good comes from its doer naturally, without affectation. Kasb in the language is the increase in the price of a sale over the price of a purchase, and this is a praiseworthy matter.

But a person may become accustomed to sin and familiar with it, and not feel shame in committing it, and perhaps even boast of it, so that it becomes for him a gain (kasb), and he does the sin as you do the obedience; that is, he feels no remorse for doing it and his soul does not reproach him for it. It is as if these people regard sin as a gain in which they rejoice. For this reason He said ﴿for what they used to earn﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 14] and did not say "yaktasibun" (what they acquire).

Therefore: the Exalted commanded the believers to forgive minor slips, repelling evil with what is better, so that perhaps the other party will desist. The Exalted said: ﴿Repel with that which is better, and behold, the one between whom and you there is enmity will become as though he were a close friend﴾ [Fussilat: 34].

The wise Lawgiver is most eager to preserve the bonds between people, even in the fiercest battles of enmity, which is killing. You see Him permit retaliation: ﴿And in retaliation there is life for you, O people of understanding...﴾ [al-Baqarah: 179]. At the same time He calls to pardon: ﴿But if anything is remitted to him by his brother...﴾ [al-Baqarah: 178]. Reflect on the word "his brother" here: despite the enmity, they are brothers: ﴿then pursuit in a fair manner and payment to him with good conduct...﴾ [al-Baqarah: 178].

We often hear someone say: "I repelled with what is better and did not get the result that Allah informed of." We say to him: In reality you did not repel with what is better, for if you had, you would have found the answer as Allah informed. But you imagined that you had repelled with what is better and made it an experiment with Allah, and experimenting with Allah is doubt.

Then the Exalted elevates the human soul to a higher rank than mere pardon, for you may forgive one who has wronged you, yet something remains in your soul against him, which calls you to rid yourself of the traces of the injury, and then He raises you to a higher rank, which is to do good to one who has wronged you: ﴿Those who restrain anger and pardon people, and Allah loves the good-doers﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 134].

Al-Hasan al-Basri was asked and he said: "The one who wrongs you makes your Lord your ally; and the one who makes my Lord my ally deserves to be rewarded. Then, moreover, he transfers his good deeds to me."

Therefore, a Sufi man, when word reached him that a man had cursed him in a gathering, sent to him a dish of fresh dates and said to his servant: "Go with it to so-and-so and say to him: My master sends you this, because you gave him your good deeds yesterday."

In our practical life we see that when one child strikes his brother, you find the father showing compassion to the one who was struck and comforting him, and rebuking and reprimanding the striker, as if the blow came for the benefit of the one struck.

Therefore: the Exalted wishes to make creation tender toward one another, which means that life is built on affection and love, not on hatred and rancour; it is built on mutual support, not on mutual opposition.

For this reason, when the scholars treated this matter, they divided the affliction that befalls a person into two kinds: an affliction in which you have an adversary, and an affliction in which you have no adversary. The first is caused by a person whom you then take as an adversary, and this is harder on the soul because it calls you to revenge.

The other is that which comes from Allah with no human hand in it, and this is easier and lighter on the soul, since there is no adversary in it. For the adversary by his nature stirs in your soul impulses of revenge every time you see him.

Therefore, in the counsel of Luqman to his son: ﴿And be patient over what befalls you; indeed, that is of the determined matters﴾ [Luqman: 17]. The intended meaning here is an affliction that befalls you from Allah. Therefore no command to forgive and overlook came with it. When He speaks of an affliction that befalls you from people, He says: ﴿But whoever is patient and forgives—indeed, that is of the matters requiring determination﴾ [al-Shura: 43], that is, he forgave the adversary. ﴿Indeed, that is of the matters requiring determination﴾ [al-Shura: 43]. Here the emphasis is increased by the lam in ﴿lamin 'azm al-umur﴾, because patience in this case is harder and requires more effort and striving than the first.

His saying at the end of the verse: ﴿That He may recompense a people for what they used to earn﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 14] indicates the justice of recompense, and that it is of the same kind as the deed. The Exalted clarified this matter in the following verse:

﴿Whoever does righteousness, it is for his own self...﴾.

Consider carefully ﴿for himself...﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 15] in righteous deeds, and against himself in evil, ﴿then to your Lord you will be returned﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 15]. It is as if the recompense, for him and against him, comes before the return to God in the Hereafter.

Yes, this is in this world, so that the balance of life's movement may be upright. For if all recompense were deferred to the Hereafter, people would find sin easy, and falling into it would be trivial for them, so falsehood would spread and evil would increase.

Therefore, some worldly punishment must occur so that affairs may be set right. For this reason, the Exalted says: ﴿And indeed for those who have done wrong is a punishment short of that...﴾ [al-Tur: 47].

And He said about the people of the Fire's punishment: ﴿And We will surely make them taste the nearer punishment...﴾ [al-Sajdah: 21], meaning: the near one in this world, ﴿short of the greater punishment; perhaps they will return﴾ [al-Sajdah: 21], that is: in the Hereafter.

This principle is clear in Surah al-Kahf, in the words of Dhul-Qarnayn: ﴿As for one who wrongs, We will punish him; then he will be returned to his Lord, and He will punish him with a terrible punishment﴾ [al-Kahf: 87].

This is a consolation for our Master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), at a time when he suffered the most severe hardship from the foremost of disbelievers among his contemporaries, in obstinacy, denial, arrogance, and harm by word and deed, by deceit and conspiracy. They left nothing that could harm the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) without doing it.

So his Lord consoles him, saying to him: You are not unprecedented in this. Your fellow prophets before you faced this same hardship and denial. Take consolation from the history of the call before you, for you came to them with the truth while they wanted falsehood, so they are bound to confront you.

He, the Exalted, says: ﴿And We had certainly given the Children of Israel the Scripture...﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 16], meaning the Torah, just as We revealed the Qur'an to you, ﴿and judgement...﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 16], meaning the standards of justice by which the affairs of creation are set right.

Judgement (al-hukm) among the Children of Israel is, for us, like the Sunnah (the prophetic tradition). For this reason, the Truth, glory be to Him, addressed the wives of the Prophet saying: ﴿And remember what is recited in your houses of the verses of Allah...﴾ [al-Ahzab: 34], meaning the Qur'an, ﴿and wisdom﴾, meaning the sayings of the Messenger of Allah.

﴿And prophethood...﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 16]: Allah, glory be to Him, placed prophethood among the Children of Israel more than among any other nation, to the extent that they boasted over the rest of the nations on this matter. In reality, it was not a cause for pride; rather, it indicated a defect in them and a fault held against them, because the abundance of prophets indicates the corruption of the people. A nation does not need a new messenger except when corruption has spread among it.

So: the abundance of prophets indicated the abundance of corruption among them. Therefore, the abundance of prophets among them is not a testimony in their favour but against them. For this reason we find them killing the prophets more than any other nation did, and for this reason we find them conspiring to kill Muhammad as well, but far be that from them.

The Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, made clear to them that this matter is specific to you and confined to your prophets only, so He restricted it to them, saying: ﴿Why did you kill the prophets of Allah before?﴾ [al-Baqarah: 91], meaning: this speech belonged to a past time; as for now, no, and you will never be able to do it.

His saying: ﴿and We provided them with good things...﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 16]. Among these good things were the manna and the quails which Allah sent down to them during the period of wandering (al-tih), when there was no settlement and no land to cultivate. Allah sent down to them the manna, which is a liquid resembling honey that falls on the leaves of trees as translucent granules dropping in the morning; its taste is sweet, as if it were a mixture of honey and cream.

As for the salwa, it is a migratory bird like the quail, and it is rich in protein. So: from the manna and the salwa He gave them complete nourishment. Yet their materialism overcame them, and they wanted to eat from what was under their hands, from what the earth produces. They said that this ready-made food might not come, for the manna might not descend and the salwa might not reach them.

For this reason they said to Moses: ﴿We will not endure one kind of food, so call upon your Lord to bring forth for us from what the earth grows: its herbs, its cucumbers, its garlic, its lentils, and its onions...﴾ [al-Baqarah: 61].

Indeed, their materialism reached the point that they asked Moses, peace be upon him, to show them the Truth, glory be to Him, saying: ﴿We will never believe you until we see Allah openly...﴾ [al-Baqarah: 55].

His saying, glory be to Him: ﴿and We preferred them over the worlds﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 16]. They said: the worlds of their own time; it is not absolute, because the Children of Israel lived in a time when disbelief and idolatry prevailed, while they were a people of Scripture who believed in Allah, so they were superior to those of their time.

Someone may ask: what is the connection between this discussion of the Jews here?

They said: Allah, glorified is He, intends to say: "Mention, O Muhammad, that your nation, Quraysh and others, have some of the traits of the Jews and have done many of their deeds, so Allah will send down upon them what He sent down upon their predecessors."

He, exalted is He, says: ﴿Do they not see that We have made a sanctuary secure, while people are being snatched away from around them?﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 67].

Anyone who went out of Makkah alone would be seized, killed, and have his wealth and belongings taken. But the people of Makkah did not dare to do this, because of their standing with the House (the Ka'bah) and their concern for the safety of their trade caravans, which travelled between Yemen and Syria and passed through most of the tribes.

Furthermore, Quraysh's service to the House and to its visitors secured their trade and protected their caravans. And why would it not, when they receive the guests of the Most Merciful (ḍuyūf al-Raḥmān) in Makkah and attend to their needs?

Therefore, we find that this matter is the link between Surat al-Fil and Surat Quraysh. Read: ﴿Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with the companions of the elephant? Did He not make their plot into misguidance? And He sent against them birds in flocks, striking them with stones of hard clay, and made them like eaten straw.﴾ [al-Fil: 1-5].

If you ask: why did God repel the companions of the elephant and make them like eaten straw? The answer is found at the beginning of Surat Quraysh: ﴿For the accustomed security of the Quraysh, their accustomed security in the caravan of winter and summer﴾ [Quraysh: 1-2]. Had the House been destroyed, Quraysh's standing would have been destroyed with it, their dignity would have been lost from the hearts of the people of the Arabian Peninsula, and they would not have been able to undertake the journey of winter and summer.

It is as if Allah, glorified is He, is saying to His Prophet (ﷺ): "I have done such and such for these people, I have defended them, and I have given them standing and rank, yet despite this they stand in hostility toward your call, because you will strip them of the tyrannical sovereignty and the oppressive dominion to which they have become accustomed."

As for His saying: ﴿And We gave them clear proofs concerning the matter...﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 17], this means: signs and indications concerning the description of the Prophet (ﷺ). The Jews went to the city of the Messenger of Allah only because they knew of his coming, knew his attributes and the time of his mission, and they used to boast of his coming and seek victory through him over the disbelievers and idolaters.

They used to say: "The time of a prophet from among the Arabs has drawn near. We will follow him and kill you with him, the killing of 'Ad and Iram." But when the Messenger of Allah was sent, they opposed him and disbelieved in his call, as Allah says: ﴿And previously they had been seeking victory over those who disbelieved; but when there came to them that which they recognised, they disbelieved in it...﴾ [al-Baqarah: 89].

He, exalted is He, also says about their recognition of the Messenger of Allah: ﴿They recognise him as they recognise their sons...﴾ [al-An'am: 20].

Therefore we saw 'Abdullah ibn Salam, who was one of the rabbis of the Jews, say: "By Allah, I recognised him when I saw him, as I recognise my son, and my recognition of Muhammad is even stronger." Despite this recognition they denied his prophethood and disbelieved in him, and they neglected the signs and indications of his prophethood that were with them. ﴿And they denied them while their souls were convinced of them, out of wrongdoing and arrogance...﴾ [al-Naml: 14].

Thus, when Allah guided 'Abdullah ibn Salam to Islam, he went to our master, the Messenger of Allah, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, Allah has opened my breast to Islam, but I fear that if I embrace Islam the Jews will blame and accuse me when they learn of it. So ask them about me, O Messenger of Allah, before they learn of my Islam."

Indeed, the Messenger of Allah asked them: "What do you say about Ibn Salam?" They said: "He is our master and the son of our master, our rabbi and the son of our rabbi." At that, 'Abdullah ibn Salam uttered the two testimonies and said: "I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and that you are the Messenger of Allah." They said: "Rather, he is such-and-such," and they began to revile and abuse him. 'Abdullah said: "Did I not tell you, O Messenger of Allah, that they are a people of deceit (buhut)?"

Strangely, when the Makkan disbelievers asked the Jews: "Are we better guided or Muhammad?" they said: "Rather, you are better guided than Muhammad." All of this is because they had a worldly authority which they wished to keep. Before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered Madinah, they were preparing Ibn Ubayy to be their king, and they had prepared a crown of kingship for him. But the Messenger of Allah preceded him. When he reached Quba' and the people of Madinah welcomed him, they found no room for that, and Ibn Ubayy kept this grievance in his heart until he died.

As for His saying: ﴿And they did not differ...﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 17], meaning: concerning the Messenger of Allah, ﴿except after knowledge had come to them...﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 17], concerning the Messenger of Allah, ﴿out of jealousy among themselves...﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 17], because some of them believed the Messenger of Allah and embraced Islam, and some of them denied him and rejected him.

Among them was one whom the Messenger of Allah praised. He said: "The best of the Jews is Mukhayriq," who was a man whose breast Allah had opened to Islam. It coincided that the Messenger went out on one of the military expeditions, and Mukhayriq went out with the Messenger of Allah and gave away all that he owned without announcing it. In that expedition Mukhayriq was killed without having performed a single prayer rak'ah to Allah.

As for His, glorified is He, saying: ﴿Indeed, your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that about which they used to differ﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 17], meaning: concerning the matter of faith in the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Meaning: We have placed you, O Muhammad, upon the straight path. The sharia (the revealed law and way) is the path that leads to water, which is the origin of life: ﴿And We made from water every living thing﴾ [al-Anbiya: 30]. Thus he named the religion "sharia."

Just as water is the life of bodies, religion is the life of souls and hearts. It is what grants them the other, everlasting life, in which they neither miss delight nor does delight miss them. This is the true life of which Allah said: ﴿O you who have believed, respond to Allah and to the Messenger when He calls you to that which gives you life﴾ [al-Anfal: 24]...

Surah 45, verse 19: That is, the disbelievers of Makkah went to his uncle Abu Talib and said: "If the son of your brother wants wealth, we will gather wealth from our own properties for him until he becomes the richest of us, and if he wants kingship, we will make him king over us." Our master, the Messenger of Allah, then gave his well-known reply: ﴿Indeed, the wrongdoers are allies of one another...﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 19]. That is, they help one another and support one another, for injustice has united them and unified their aims. ﴿And Allah is the ally of the righteous﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 19]. That is, in contrast, Allah is the ally of the righteous: He helps them, supports them, and gives them victory. These are among the antitheses that add clarity to the meaning.

The word بَصَائِرُ is the plural of بصيرة (basirah, inner insight), which is what exists in a person's conscience of the light of truth. Sight perceives material things, while insight perceives non-material things and values and distinguishes between them.

So its place is the heart: it is a light that God casts into the heart of His servant. We say: "So-and-so has basirah," meaning he has penetrating insight into matters, and he can foresee a thing so that it comes about in accordance with his foresight.

Guidance (al-hudā, or al-hidāyah) is to reach the truth by the nearest and easiest path for you, for there is no hardship in guidance. Therefore God described the believers by His saying: ﴿Those are upon guidance from their Lord﴾ [al-Baqarah: 5]. They are upon guidance, as if it were a mount carrying them to their goal and to what the Truth intends from them.

وَرَحْمَةٌ (wa-raḥmah, "and mercy"): all of these are attributes of the Noble Qur'an. It is insight for mankind, it is guidance, and it is mercy. In another verse He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And We send down from the Qur'an that which is a healing and a mercy for the believers﴾ [al-Isra': 82].

We have said that there is a difference between healing (shifā') and mercy (raḥmah). Healing means the existence of an illness that the Qur'an treats, or a crookedness that the Qur'an straightens and corrects in its course. The Qur'an mends what is in us of deficiency, of negligence, of heedlessness, and of deviation, and sets our course back onto the right path and into constructive movement.

It is like the student who turns away from his lessons: he fails and falls short, but if he returns to what is right and studies, he succeeds as well. Likewise, if we neglect the Book of our Lord and His method, diseases afflict us; if we return to it, it heals us. As for mercy, it means that the disease does not come at all.

As for His saying, glory be to Him: ﴿This is insight for mankind, and guidance and mercy for a people who are certain﴾, meaning: this effect of the Qur'an occurs only for those who are certain, the believers in it and in its truthfulness, and that it is the true method that contains light, guidance, healing and mercy.

The verb ﴿حَسِبَ﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 21], with the vowel of the sin pronounced with a kasra, means "thought" (ẓanna). There is also ḥasiba with a fatḥa, which comes from ḥisāb, meaning "reckoning" or "counting." The phrase ﴿ٱجْتَرَحُواْ ٱلسَّيِّئَاتِ﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 21] means that they committed them and acquired them. For this reason, birds of prey that hunt are called (al-kawāsib, "those that earn") in the sense that they are used for hunting, so they are kawāsib. The sayyi'ah (evil deed) is everything that harms its doer, harming him through punishment or blame.

The verse contains a rhetorical question that conveys denial and astonishment at this assumption. How could We equate the disbelievers with the believers, or the obedient with the disobedient? Those who turned away from your call, O Muhammad, and thought that We would treat them as equal to those who believed, their assumption is mistaken.

Far apart are this and that. We will not treat them as We treat you. Rather, We treat them in this world with defeat, and We treat you with victory and empowerment. We treat them in the Hereafter with punishment, and We treat you with bliss and reward.

﴿سَوَآءً مَّحْيَاهُمْ وَمَمَاتُهُمْ﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 21] means: We do not equate you with them, neither in the life of this world nor in the Hereafter. ﴿سَآءَ مَا يَحْكُمُونَ﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 21] means that whoever judges by equality here has a bad judgment and it is void, because it is an unjust ruling that contradicts truth and justice.

Thus their assumption is what led them to ruin and drove them to disbelieve in you. Had they been certain that the end is different and the recompense is different, they would have believed and done righteous deeds.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 45, verse 22:

After the Mighty and Majestic had spoken of the unjust and mistaken assumption of the disbelievers, namely that We would make them equal to those who believe, [He explained the wrong in this assumption].

Having made clear the nature of the injustice in this assumption, He now speaks to us here of His justice, and of the balance of truth (al-haqq) by which the heavens and the earth were established at the beginning, before He created man, and before the believer and the disbeliever came into being.

So God created the heavens and the earth with truth, and brought them into being with precise reckoning and absolute justice. The justice of heaven is not limited to the recompense of the Hereafter, each according to his deed; rather, it is an eternal justice by which the process of creation was established.

﴿And God created the heavens and the earth in truth, and so that every soul may be recompensed for what it has earned, and they will not be wronged﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 22]. Truth (al-haqq) is the thing that is firm and does not change. When we look at the signs of God in the universe, its heaven and its earth, we find them to be firm signs moving by a precise, well-ordered system that never fails and never changes, because they were built from the beginning upon truth.

It is as if God, exalted is He, is giving us a signal and drawing our attention to the fact that the movement of our life in this world will never be upright, and will never proceed in peace, unless it is founded upon truth and built upon the balance of truth, by which the heavens and the earth were established.

Read, for example: ﴿The sun and the moon [move] by a reckoning﴾ [al-Rahman: 5], i.e., they were created with precise calculation.

﴿And the star and the tree prostrate themselves. And the heaven He raised up, and He set up the balance﴾ [al-Rahman: 6-7].

And reflect on the conclusion of the verse: ﴿and so that every soul may be recompensed for what it has earned, and they will not be wronged﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 22]. Since the matter rests upon truth, justice in recompense must necessarily be realized, and injustice must be eliminated.

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says: "Have you seen the one who has taken his own desire as his god...?"

The ilah (deity) is the object of worship to whom your whole life is devoted to serving what He wants from you. The word ma'bud (object of worship) is a general term applied to the one worshipped in truth, who is Allah, the Exalted, the Creator, the Provider, the Originator of this universe, and it is applied to false objects of worship, such as those who worshipped idols, the sun, or the moon.

These and others are false objects of worship that neither harm nor benefit, and only the ignorant worship them to satisfy the emotion of religiosity within them. They want a religion without obligations and a god without commands or prohibitions.

Among these false deities is desire (hawa). Some people take their desire as their god, and desire in itself is blameworthy. Therefore it has been said: "The bane of opinion is desire."

When the Truth, glory be to Him, praised His Messenger, He said: "Nor does he speak from desire" [al-Najm: 3]...

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, makes clear that the one who has taken his desire as his god is a lost person, "and Allah has led him astray knowingly." That is: He judged him to be astray because He made him one who chooses. He chose his desire. Had He made him compelled, like the heavens and the earth, he would not have been able to disobey. We have said that Allah wants from us the heart, not the mere form; He wants us to come to Him willingly.

The Truth, glory be to Him, says: "And a soul and He who proportioned it, and inspired it with its wickedness and its righteousness" [ash-Shams: 7-8]. So, when he chose misguidance and Allah, the Exalted, found him astray, He judged him from eternity to be astray, and reality came as the Truth, glory be to Him, had judged and as Allah had known of him.

Therefore we have said: the angels continue to marvel when they see the reality of life conforming to what was written in the Preserved Tablet, and they say: "What an excellent Lord!"

The meaning of "Have you seen" (a-fa-ra'ayta) is: Have you known, whether you saw it with your eyes or not, as in His saying, the Exalted: "Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with the companions of the elephant?" [al-Fil: 1], that is, "Did you not know?", because the Messenger of Allah was born in that year and did not see the incident of the elephant.

As for His saying, the Exalted: "And He has sealed over their hearing and their hearts, and placed over their eyes a covering" — the meaning of "sealed" (khatama) is: struck and obliterated. Here He gathered all the means of perception in the human soul: the ear, which hears the verses of Allah, hears the eloquence of the speech of Allah, His promise and His warning; the eye, which sees the cosmic signs, contemplates them and draws evidence from them of their Creator and Originator; and the heart, the seat of belief.

Allah sealed all these means only because their owner loved disbelief and found comfort in misguidance, so Allah helped him in what he loves, and sealed these faculties so that disbelief does not come out of them and faith does not enter them. And how can one believe who does not hear the speech of Allah, does not see His signs in the universe, and whose heart does not incline to the delight of faith in Allah?

Therefore He said at the end of the verse: "So who can guide him after Allah?" No one possesses his guidance, as He said elsewhere: "And whomever Allah leaves astray, for him there is no guide" [Ghafir: 33].

This is a denial from them of the Last Day, but the truth must surface in the "slips" (fultat) of the tongue. Their describing the life they live as "dunya" (the lower, worldly life) is evidence and an acknowledgment from them that there is another life, more noble and higher than this one.

As in their saying: ﴿Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of Allah...﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 7]. They thereby acknowledge that he (ﷺ) is the Messenger of Allah, even though they are hostile to him and disbelievers in his call.

And their saying: ﴿We die and we live...﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 24] means: we die, and our sons live after us. This is because they do not believe in life after death; so the life they mean is the continuation of their sons after them.

﴿And nothing destroys us but time...﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 24], i.e., time is what causes us to die. It is well known that time is a container for events, and it is a creation of Allah, Exalted, which does not cause death; rather, it is Allah who causes death. In the sacred hadith: i.e., its Creator and its Owner.

﴿And they have no knowledge of that; they only conjecture﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 24]. Since they have no knowledge of that, why would Allah punish them? They said: He punishes them because they rejected the knowledge that came to them from their Lord through the tongues of the Messengers. ﴿They only conjecture﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 24], i.e., they are merely conjecturing in their saying: ﴿It is nothing but our worldly life; we die and we live, and nothing destroys us but time...﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 24].

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿And when Our verses are recited to them as clear evidences...﴾.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 45, verse 25:

The disbelievers did not have a single proof that held up. Rather, they had many arguments which they advanced in order to evade faith in Allah, His Messenger and His Qur'an. Therefore, when the signs of Allah are recited to them, that is, the verses of the Qur'an, you find for them many varied arguments.

Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿When Our signs are recited to them, they say: "We have heard. If we willed, we could say the like of this..."﴾ [al-Anfal: 31].

In another verse He says: ﴿When Our clear signs are recited to them, those who do not expect to meet Us say: "Bring us a Qur'an other than this, or change it..."﴾ [Yunus: 15].

So they make two demands. The first demand: they want a Qur'an other than the one Allah has sent down. The second demand: they want one verse to be substituted for another. They demanded the removal of the verses that mock the idols, and likewise the verses that threaten them with an evil end.

Just as they attacked the Qur'an and wanted to change and alter it, they attacked the Messenger of Allah to whom this Qur'an was sent down, and they said: ﴿When Our clear signs are recited to them, they say: "This is none but a man who wants to turn you away from what your fathers used to worship." And they say: "This is nothing but a fabricated lie." And those who disbelieved say of the truth when it came to them: "This is nothing but evident magic."﴾ [Saba': 43].

Arguments following arguments, and their aim is that they will not believe, while they know that all their arguments are fallen and have no foundation. Someone may ask: If Allah cites their arguments in several verses of His Qur'an, why does He say in the verse of Surah al-Jathiyah: ﴿Their argument was only that they said: "Bring us our fathers..."﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 25]?

Why did He restrict their argument here with (mā kāna) and (illā)?

If we reflect on all the previous arguments, we will find them merely (talākīk) — pretexts — so that they would not believe. But their main argument, which was原 rooted in them and in their thinking, is that they did not believe in resurrection after death.

Therefore Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Their argument was only that they said: "Bring us our fathers..."﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 25].

The Almighty, Glorified is He, also said: ﴿Indeed, these say: "There is only our first death, and we will not be resurrected. So bring our fathers, if you are truthful."﴾ [al-Dukhan: 34-36].

Among them was one who would hold old, decayed bones in his hand, rub them until they became dust and scattered, and say: ﴿"When we have become bones and crumbled remains, will we indeed be resurrected in a new creation?"﴾ [al-Isra': 49].

They considered resurrection after death far-fetched, because they overlooked the beginning of existence and the beginning of the creation of man. If we counted the population of the world, we would find it increasing as we move forward and decreasing as we go back, and so on until we reach the origin of man, the original source, which is Adam and Eve. From where did they come into existence? This is an unseen matter which they had to reflect upon.

The Qur'an has responded to their denial of resurrection and their saying: ﴿"When we have become bones and crumbled remains, will we indeed be resurrected in a new creation?"﴾ [al-Isra': 49], with His words: ﴿Say: "Is there any of your partners who originates creation and then repeats it?" Say: "Allah originates creation and then repeats it; so how are you deluded?"﴾ [Yunus: 34].

Indeed Allah, glorified is He, is alone capable of that. So how do you invert the realities, when you know the reality and deny it with deliberate lying?

These are ﴿When Our signs are recited to them...﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 25], that is: when the verses of the Qur'an, clear in their meaning, are recited to them.

﴿Their argument was only...﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 25], meaning: they found no argument by which to justify their obstinacy and denial, ﴿except that they said: "Bring us our fathers..."﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 25], that is, those who have died, if you are truthful.

This is a demand that shows their bankruptcy and obstinacy; they have no logic or argument that justifies this stubbornness.

Therefore Allah responded to them, saying:

﴿Say: "Allah gives you life, then causes you to die..."﴾.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 45, verse 26:

That is: Say to them, O Muhammad, ﴿Allah gives you life, then causes you to die⦆, that is, in this world; ﴿then He will gather you⦆, after resurrection and rising up, ﴿to the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt⦆, that is, there is no doubt in it; ﴿but most of mankind do not know⦆. Thus He negated knowledge from them.

Their knowledge falls short of grasping the realities of things. Just as creation is one of the signs of Allah, so too death is one of the signs of Allah, which we see and touch every day. As long as you accept the sign of creation and the sign of death, and see them and do not doubt them,

then when we tell you that after this life there is another life, then believe, for the One who owns these signs is one, and the premises which you judge to be true must lead to a conclusion which you also judge to be true, and here are the premises before you, true.

﴿Say: Allah gives you life⦆: that is, He gives the one who is brought to life the strength by which he performs the task for which he was created. The first giving of life was in Adam, when his Lord created him, formed him, and breathed into him of His spirit, then brought us into being from his offspring.

In another verse the Truth, glorified be He, says: ﴿How can you disbelieve in Allah, when you were dead and He gave you life⦆ [al-Baqarah: 28].

Your disbelief has no proof or reasoning behind it, for the matter of bringing to life from non-existence, and creation, is a matter that does not admit of dispute. Where was Adam before Allah created him, and where were you? ﴿Has there come upon man a period of time when he was not a thing worth mentioning?⦆ [al-Insan: 1], that is, he had no existence.

So the matter of life and death cannot be disputed by anyone, for Allah, glorified and exalted be He, created us from non-existence, and no one has ever claimed that he created mankind or created himself.

As for His saying, exalted be He, ﴿then He causes you to die⦆: no one doubts that he will die. Death is decreed upon all people. Creation from non-existence is established by proof, and death is established by sense perception and observation.

Therefore, it is among the mercies of Allah toward human reason, regarding unseen events, that Allah, glorified be He, has brought them near to us through something observed. How? The Truth, blessed and exalted be He, has told us about a stage of creation which we did not witness, but death is something we have all witnessed.

Since death is witnessed by us, the Truth, glorified be He, brings it forward as evidence for the stages of creation which we did not witness; death is the negation of life.

Then the Truth, glorified be He, says: ﴿Then He will gather you to the Day of Resurrection⦆. The gathering here means after resurrection, restoration and bringing back to life from death. It is the Day of Gathering. Allah, exalted be He, says: ﴿And thus We have revealed to you an Arabic Qur'an that you may warn the Mother of Cities and those around it, and warn of the Day of Gathering, about which there is no doubt⦆ [al-Shura: 7], that is, you may frighten them of this day, which is the Day of Resurrection. The gathering on this day will occur in several respects: the resurrection, in which the body and spirit are joined; the gathering of the angels of the higher assembly with mankind; the gathering of the oppressor and the oppressed; and the follower and the followed.

He, exalted be He, says: ﴿Allah—there is no god but Him. He will surely gather you to the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt. And who is more truthful in statement than Allah?⦆ [al-Nisa': 87].

Then the Truth, glorified be He, says:

﴿And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth...⦆.

Here is the translation of the passage.

Here the style is one of restriction (qasr) through fronting the prepositional phrase, which conveys that ownership of the heavens and the earth belongs to Allah alone, with no partner: ﴿And on the day the Hour is established...﴾ [al-Jathiya: 27]. The Hour is established as though it had been sleeping and then rose. He left the Hour indefinite so that we would await it at any moment.

Indefiniteness here, as we have said, is itself a form of clarification (ʿayn al-bayan), for it keeps us always prepared for it, just as Allah the Exalted left a person's term (ajal) indefinite so that he would always keep it in mind at every time and not be heedless of it. Whoever does not possess for himself survival for the blink of an eye is deserving of not being heedless of his afterlife and of being wary lest his term arrive while he is in disobedience to Allah.

Whoever dies upon something is raised upon it, especially if death does not await causes. Death without causes is itself the cause: he died because he is mortal and his term has come. The poets were alert to this meaning, and one of them said:

In death there is what defeats, and in its causes;
every person is a pledge held in the folding of his book.

A lion, by your life, one who dies by his claw
at the encounter is like one who dies by his fang.

If he sleeps on you, then what benefit is any seeking?
And if he does not sleep, then medicine is among its tails.

Yes, a man enters the operating room and does not come out of it, and medicine becomes the cause of his death. So: Allah, glorified is He, leaves things indefinite for a wisdom and a purpose. And among His mercy toward His creation is that, when He made the Hour indefinite, He appointed for it signs that alert the heedless, so that people will not be taken by surprise.

Among His mercy toward us is that He made for it minor signs and major signs; this is tenderness from Allah toward His creation: ﴿None will reveal it at its time except Him. It has weighed heavily upon the heavens and the earth. It will not come to you except suddenly...﴾ [al-A'raf: 187].

As for His saying: ﴿On that day the falsifiers will lose﴾ [al-Jathiya: 27], i.e., those who persist in falsehood. The word (yakhsar) comes from loss (al-khusran), which is opposed to gain (al-maksab), and this is a matter known to merchants, for every merchant seeks gain, i.e., increase over capital.

So: every deed must be reckoned in terms of gain and loss. The disbeliever in this world thinks his deed will return to him as gain in this world, but he will be taken by surprise on the Day of Resurrection, when the time for work has ended, to find that his deed has returned to him as loss. ﴿On the day every soul will find what it did of good present, and what it did of evil, it will wish that between it and that were a distant term...﴾ [Al 'Imran: 30].

The meaning of loss here is that he finds all his deeds gone as scattered dust without benefit: ﴿And those who disbelieved, their deeds are like a mirage in a level plain, which the thirsty one thinks is water, until, when he comes to it, he finds it to be nothing; and he finds Allah with him, so He pays him his account in full. And Allah is swift in reckoning﴾ [al-Nur: 39].

Therefore, when we were asked about the owners of inventions and innovations that served humanity, made the movement of life easier for people, and eased the pains of those in pain: how, after all this, do they enter the Fire?

I said: Yes, because they performed these deeds to serve humanity and Allah was not in their minds. Therefore they took their wages from humankind, as honor and as perpetuation of their memory and glorification of them; they made statues for them and authored books about them, and so on.

So: they have no share in the reward of the Hereafter. Had they done these deeds for Allah, they would have found their reward with Allah, for the hired worker seeks his wage only from the one for whom he worked.

Therefore the disbeliever will be taken by surprise by this reality. We understand this surprise from His saying: ﴿and he finds Allah with him, so He pays him his account in full...﴾ [al-Nur: 39]. He is surprised by a God who was not in his mind, or whom he denied and disbelieved in.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 45, verse 28:

That is: on the Day of Resurrection you will see every nation kneeling (jathiyah), from the verb jatha, yajtha, jathwan, meaning he sat down on his knees, or he stood on the tips of his toes. This is the posture of one who is fearful, humbled and abased. From the same root is the Almighty's saying: ﴿Then We will surely bring them forth around Hell, kneeling (jithiyyan)﴾ [Maryam: 68].

Close to it is the verb jathama, yajthumu, jathuman, meaning he remained in his place or clung to the ground. From it is the Almighty's saying: ﴿So they were found lying prone (jathimin) in their homes﴾ [Hud: 94].

So the situation is a grievous one, a situation of terror, horror and panic, such that people cannot remain seated on their seats, so they sit on their knees. If the horror intensifies, they stand on the tips of their toes, and this is the stance of one who awaits danger and dread. As for natural sitting, it allows a person to settle his buttocks on the ground, and it is the state of tranquillity.

There is a difference between qu'ud (sitting/remaining seated) and julus (sitting down), even though the outcome is one. Qu'ud comes after standing: one says, "He was standing, then he qa'ada (sat down)." Julus comes from a state of lying down: "He was lying down, then he jalasa (sat up)."

So here is a philosophical point: qu'ud comes from a higher posture, which is standing, and julus from a lower posture, which is lying down. Sitting or qu'ud ensures a person comfort, since most of his body rests on the ground, and he is at ease, unlike the standing person, for example, whom his feet bear.

Therefore, if you stand for a long time you become tired and alternate your weight between your feet while standing. Then the load on the feet increases if you add walking to standing, then it increases further if you add to walking something you carry, and so on.

So when a person becomes tired, the first thing he does is put down the load he is carrying, so that the weight on his feet is lightened. Then he stops walking to reduce the effort, then he sits, and after that he lies down, casting his whole body onto the ground, and this posture ensures the utmost rest for the body.

But this Qur'anic depiction in the words jathiyah or jathimah does not indicate rest. It indicates submission, abasement, humiliation and the intensity of fear that makes a person, God forbid, cling to the ground, or kneel from the intensity of his fear.

The Almighty thus depicts this situation through words that make you feel the horror of the situation and the intensity of its distress. It is up to you to imagine the situation and to take it as an experience you have actually passed through, in a dreadful situation in which each person is preoccupied with himself.

So the Resurrection has come: "qamat" (has arisen), meaning it will not sit down again, while the nation is kneeling. All of them, believer and disbeliever, are kneeling, awaiting what will happen. No one here is above the law (there is no "jastana" [a cheat]). Fear and horror overwhelm everyone, and all await the word of truth.

﴿Every nation will be called to its record...﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 28]. Here the record is attributed to the nation, and for this reason the Orientalists stopped at this verse objecting, because the Almighty says in another verse: ﴿This is Our record; it speaks against you with truth...﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 29].

So once He attributes the record to the nation, and once to Himself. Had they understood God, they would have found no ground for objection.

The meaning of "Our record" is that which We commanded the recording angels to write, so that it would be a proof against its owner on the Day of Resurrection, and We say to him: ﴿Read your record; sufficient is your own soul today as a reckoner against you﴾ [al-Isra': 14].

It is also their record, meaning that which was written against them, in which their deeds were registered. So every word has its meaning and its significance, and it is well known in the style of the Qur'an that it uses a word here in one sense and there in another sense.

The Qur'an as a whole requires reflection, contemplation, and knowledge of the occasions of revelation and the circumstances of the verses. Consider, for example, the Almighty's saying: ﴿And do not give the foolish your property...﴾ [al-Nisa': 5]. The safih (foolish person) is one who does not handle his property well, so the Lawgiver did not make property his; rather, in a state of foolishness, the property belongs to his guardian.

Therefore He said "your property" (amwalakum), although it is the right of this foolish person, because believers' blood is equal and the least of them may extend protection on their behalf.

So we take the property of the foolish person and preserve it for him until we perceive in him maturity (rushd), and then we hand over his property to him so that he may dispose of it himself. Thus, when He mentions it again, He says: ﴿But if you perceive in them maturity, then hand over to them their property...﴾ [al-Nisa': 6], attributing it to them because it has become their possession and they have freedom to dispose of it.

And the Almighty's saying: ﴿Today...﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 28], that is, on the Day of Resurrection, ﴿you will be recompensed for what you used to do﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 28]. So the recompense is of the same kind as the deed.

This is the Tafsir al-Sha'rawi commentary on Surah 45, verse 29.

His saying: ﴿This is Our Book...﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 29], i.e., the Book of deeds, ﴿speaks against you with truth...﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 29]. It is known that speech is by the tongue, for it is the first means of expression, and the tongue here is the tongue of state (lisan al-hal). Although the book in reality is read and does not speak, this Book, because of how clearly it manifests the truth, is as if it speaks and bears witness against its owner.

﴿Indeed, We used to have it copied what you used to do﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 29]. The meaning of nastansikh is "to record" (nuthbit): that We take from it another copy which We give to the owner of the book so that he may read it and be made aware of what he sent forward in his worldly life.

As we say, for example: "original and copy" (asl wa surah), so We give him a copy of his book and of his deeds, so that it may be a proof against him.

Among the meanings of naskh (copying) is the recording that leaves nothing out, and does not neglect any small or great thing except that it has counted it. The Exalted said: ﴿On the Day every soul will find what it did of good present, and what it did of evil, it will wish that between itself and that there were a great distance﴾ [Aal 'Imran: 30]. And He said: ﴿Not a word does he utter except that with him is an observer, ready﴾ [Qaf: 18].

The Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 45, verse 30:

Since we are discussing the book of deeds that a person reads, this verse speaks of the first type, the believer who did righteous deeds. He takes his book in his right hand, finds it in its best form, and rejoices in it and takes pride in it.

The Exalted explained this verse in another verse: ﴿As for him who is given his record in his right hand, he will say, "Here, read my record! Indeed, I was certain that I would meet my account." So he will be in a pleasant life, in an elevated garden, its fruits near at hand. "Eat and drink with satisfaction for what you did in the days past."﴾ [al-Haqqah: 19-24].

Consider here the phrase ﴿in His mercy...﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 30]. It is as if mercy were a container into which He admits them and which encompasses them. Mercy overwhelms them and surrounds them on every side. Here they will have nothing but mercy, because in the world they toiled, bore the burdens of worship and righteous deeds, and alternated between blessing and hardship, gain and loss, health and sickness. Here, however, they will find nothing but the mercy of God, which covers and embraces them.

The phrase ﴿those who believed and did righteous deeds...﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 30] shows that inner faith alone is not sufficient; rather, it must bear fruit. The fruit and benefit of faith is that you put it to work in serving the One in whom you believe.

For this reason the Qur'an always links faith with righteous deeds, as in His saying: ﴿By time, indeed mankind is in loss, except for those who believe and do righteous deeds...﴾ [al-'Asr: 1-3], because belief in God, in the Resurrection, the Reckoning, and the divine decree (al-qada' wa-l-qadar, God's predestination and decree) makes a person certain that he will be called to account and held responsible for every shortcoming.

Since you will be questioned, you must be alert, neither belittling any sin however small, nor shunning any good however slight. Whoever's ultimate end is reckoning should be careful not to let these matters slip by except through forgetfulness or heedlessness, and forgetfulness and heedlessness are remedied by seeking forgiveness and repentance.

We have said that it is among the mercies of the Truth toward creation that He legislated repentance for them. The mere legislation of repentance and the opening of its door to people is a mercy: a mercy to the negligent sinner, and a mercy to the society that suffers from the sins of sinners.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿That...﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 30] refers to the entry of the people of faith and righteous deeds into His mercy. ﴿That is the clear triumph﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 30], the evident success that encompasses complete benefit, such that nothing enters it that contradicts the truth of mercy. Then, in contrast:

﴿As for those who disbelieved...﴾.

These are in contrast to those who believed. These are the ones who take their record in their left hands. Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿But as for him who is given his record in his left hand, he will say, "Oh, I wish I had not been given my record, and had not known my account. Oh, I wish it had been the end of me!"﴾ [al-Haqqah: 25-27].

So the recompense of these people is the Fire. But before they enter it, they must be reproached and rebuked with this rebuke, and it must be made clear to them that they have no excuse for not believing. The clear signs came to them, and the Messengers came to them. We did not fall short in their regard, we did not leave them neglected, we did not seize them unawares, and we called them and showed compassion to them for as long as we called them.

We note that these people combined arrogance toward the truth with criminal conduct. Arrogance means rejecting the truth and refusing to accept it from the one who brought it, who is the Messenger. Would that they had stopped at this point and left people alone. Instead, they went beyond it to criminal conduct, which is to mock and ridicule the one who believed.

This matter was explained in His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who committed crime used to laugh at those who believed. And when they passed by them, they would exchange winks﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 29-30], meaning mockery and ridicule.

Then: ﴿And when they returned to their families, they returned jesting﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 31]. This shows that he and his family are equal in criminality, and that corruption encompasses all of them.

We see this kind of people in every age. We see them mocking those who pray or those who imitate our master, the Messenger of God, and we hear from them words of ridicule, even though they read this verse along with us.

But Allah, glorified is He, reassures the people of faith and says to them: Do not be concerned about what they inflict on you in this world, and wait for what will happen in the Hereafter: ﴿So today those who believed will laugh at the disbelievers, upon couches, observing. Have the disbelievers been rewarded for what they used to do?﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 34-36]. We say: Yes, our Lord, You have recompensed them for what they deserved.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 45, verse 32:

These are another type of those who deny the resurrection. The first type is certain and affirms that there is no resurrection and no reckoning, whereas these have not reached the stage of certainty; rather, they suppose that there is a resurrection. Supposition (zann) is when one inclines toward one thing over another.

We have previously explained that relations (nisab) are of five kinds: knowledge (ʿilm), ignorance (jahl), doubt (shakk), supposition (ẓann), and delusion (wahm). Supposition is when you favour the thing you suppose. Delusion is when you favour falsehood.

So there is something you affirm with conviction, and something you do not affirm with conviction. What you affirm and support with evidence is certain knowledge (ʿilm yaqīn). What you cannot support with evidence is not certain knowledge but imitation (taqlīd), as when a child says: ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾ [al-Ikhlas: 1].

This is true, but the child cannot prove it, nor can something be said such that the one who says it affirms it with conviction while it does not correspond to reality; that is ignorance (jahl).

Knowledge (ʿilm) is a proposition affirmed with conviction, which corresponds to reality and for which there is evidence, in contrast to ignorance (jahl), which is a proposition affirmed with conviction for which there is no evidence.

Supposition (ẓann) is the equal weighting of two relations, affirmative and negative, such that you cannot affirm either of them with conviction, for if one side prevails it becomes an outweighed proposition, and an outweighed proposition is doubt (shakk), supposition (ẓann) or delusion (wahm). Thus ẓann is the preponderance of one relation over the other, while shakk is the equality of the two sides.

Meaning: their evil deeds in the world will become apparent to them. ﴿And what they used to mock surrounded them.﴾ Meaning: it encompassed them, so they will find no escape from it and no way of flight, ﴿that which they used to mock.﴾

The passage is a commentary on Surah al-Jathiyah (45), verse 34.

Here one should reflect on the gentleness and mercy of Allah even toward His enemies and those who disbelieve in Him. The verb ﴿وَقِيلَ..﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 34] is in the passive voice (mabni lil-majhul), so it does not say "Allah said." Among His mercy toward them is that He does not confront them directly with this reality: ﴿ٱلْيَوْمَ..﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 34], that is, the Day of Resurrection, ﴿نَنسَاكُمْ..﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 34].

Almighty Allah does not forget. The meaning is: We will leave you in punishment, neglected, and We will not turn toward you with mercy, just as people leave a matter and it does not occur to their minds, because if it occurred to them, mercy toward them might have moved them.

Then Allah explains the reason for this forgetting: ﴿كَمَا نَسِيتُمْ لِقَآءَ يَوْمِكُمْ هَـٰذَا..﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 34], meaning: We forget you in the punishment just as you forgot this day and as you abandoned working for it. ﴿وَمَأْوَاكُمُ ٱلنَّارُ..﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 34]. Al-ma'wa (refuge, dwelling) is the place to which a person returns in order to rest from fatigue or to be safe from fear. So what then if the refuge of these people is the Fire, their resting place and their end? What would their condition be?

And above all this: ﴿وَمَا لَكُمْ مِّن نَّاصِرِينَ﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 34]. This is a severing of hope in salvation and a despairing of them. In this refuge they will find no one who can rescue them from it, or who will show compassion to them and lighten the punishment for them. Rather, on the contrary, they will disown you and leave you in the punishment; indeed, they will precede you into it, as He said regarding Pharaoh: ﴿يَقْدُمُ قَوْمَهُ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَامَةِ فَأَوْرَدَهُمُ ٱلنَّارَ..﴾ [Hud: 98]. ("He will lead his people on the Day of Resurrection and bring them down to the Fire...")

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 45, verse 35:

﴿That is because you took the signs of Allah in mockery...﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 35] meaning: that which has descended upon you and befallen you of punishment, its cause is your evil deeds in the world. So it is a fitting recompense, and We did not wrong them an atom's weight. ﴿That is because you took the signs of Allah in mockery...﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 35] meaning: mocked at, so they denied them, disbelieved in them, and ridiculed them.

The word ﴿mockery...﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 35] is an intensification of ridicule, as you say: "So-and-so is just (ʿadil) and so-and-so is justice (ʿadl)." That is, he is justice itself.

﴿And the life of this world deceived you...﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 35] meaning: it deceived you with its adornment, its delight, and its glitter, so you worked for it and forgot to work for the Hereafter. ﴿So today they will not be brought out from it...﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 35] meaning: from the Fire.

﴿Nor will they be allowed to make amends﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 35]. It is from the verb ʿatiba (to reproach), and reproach (ʿitab) occurs only between loved ones. Therefore they said: "Affection remains as long as reproach remains." When you wrong a friend, for example, he comes to you and reproaches you, wanting to hear from you an apology or an excuse in order to preserve your affection, because he does not want a severance between you.

It is said: "So-and-so was asked to make amends (istaʿtaba), and so he appeased him (aʿtabahu)." That is, he removed the cause of his reproach. This hamza is called hamzat al-izalah (the hamza of removal). The poet said:

As for reproach, it wears away among loved ones, while love is restored and made sincere through reproach.

Likewise, when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returned from Ta'if after its people had harmed him, he sat communing with his Lord: "If You are not angry with me, I do not mind, but Your well-being is more expansive for me. I seek Your pleasure until You are pleased." 

That is, "For You, O Lord, is what I can use to remove Your reproach," meaning: blame for something He deemed a shortcoming.

So: aʿtabahu means he removed his reproach, like aʿjama al-harf, meaning he removed its ambiguity (ʿujmah). You know that Arabic letters were originally written without dots, relying on the pure Arabic linguistic faculty that could discern the intended letter. When this faculty weakened among people, they needed dots to understand the intended meaning.

So Almighty Allah says of these people ﴿nor will they be allowed to make amends﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 35]: no reproach from them is accepted, no excuse for them is accepted, and no intercession on their behalf is accepted. If they seek to please Allah Most High by any means, it is rejected and not accepted, even repentance, because it will not benefit them on this Day.

First, the phrase (لله الحمد) (*lillahi al-hamd*) is a nominal sentence made up of a *mubtada'* (subject) and a *khabar* (predicate). Here the predicate has been placed first, which gives the sense of *qasr* (restriction), meaning that praise belongs to Allah alone. So praise is due to Allah the Exalted before anything else. It is due to Him because He created from nothing, sustained those who had ceased to exist, and guided people by His clear signs to the path of truth.

Praise is due to Allah for His self-subsistence (*qayyumiyyah*), for the method by which He guided us, and for the abode of recompense in which He rewards the believer and punishes the disbeliever. Praise is due to Him for having given us life by a spirit from Him, which revived our material existence in this world, and a spirit from Him, which revived our values in the Hereafter.

For this reason He addressed us while we were living, saying: ﴿O you who believe, respond to Allah and to the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life...﴾ [al-Anfal: 24]. The life meant here is the life of values, which grants you everlasting life in the Hereafter.

﴿And indeed, the Hereafter is the [true] life, if only they knew﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 64].

That is, it is the real life, the one worth working for.

Among the blessings of Allah that call for praise is that He taught us how to praise Him with this light word on the tongue, which the learned and the unlettered pronounce alike. Everyone says: "Al-hamdu lillah." Everyone extols Allah with one and the same expression. Had this equality not existed, the learned, the eloquent, and those possessing fluency and clarity of expression would have prevailed, while the unlettered who cannot speak well and the stammerer who cannot express himself would have lost out.

For this reason our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), drew our attention to this matter when he said, in praise of Allah the Exalted: the meaning of ﴿So to Allah belongs all praise...﴾ [al-Ḥāthiyah: 36] is that praise is a right of Allah, enduring, never ceasing or coming to an end, neither from the one who praises nor from that for which He is praised.

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, gives the reason (*hay'thiyyah*) for praising Allah: ﴿Lord of the heavens and Lord of the earth, Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-Ḥāthiyah: 36]. The *rabb* is the one who nurtures, owns, and bestows. So how could He not be praised?

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 45, verse 37:

This is another reason why praise belongs to Allah: that He, glory be to Him, is characterized by the attribute of greatness (al-kibriya'). Al-kibriya' is magnificence, majesty and dominance. Moreover, the style here is one of restriction (qasr): ﴿And to Him belongs greatness in the heavens and the earth﴾. That is, to Him alone. This is among the greatest of Allah's blessings upon us, so that we do not become slaves to anyone other than Him.

So Allah did not make you His servant except that He might spare you servitude to others. Were it not for this greatness of Allah, the Most High, we would be slaves to every powerful person and to everyone we need, even the blacksmith and the carpenter who handles your affair could enslave you.

Therefore, the meaning of ﴿And to Him belongs greatness in the heavens and the earth﴾ is as if He were saying to you: "Be at ease, O My servant, you will not become a slave to other than Me. Greatness, majesty and magnificence belong to Me alone, and I am for you all, and all creation are My dependents, and the dearest of them to Me are the most merciful to My dependents..."

The sacred hadith (hadith qudsi) confirms this attribute as belonging to Allah alone. He, glory be to Him, said in the sacred hadith: "Greatness is My cloak and majesty is My garment; whoever contends with Me over either of them, I will cast him into the Fire."

Why? Because He did not create this creation and is not entrusted with it. Therefore, a person does not act arrogantly toward creation unless his soul is veiled from remembering the greatness of the Truth, glory be to Him. Indeed, one who constantly keeps in his soul the greatness of Allah is ashamed to be arrogant, or to contend with his Lord over this attribute...

As for His saying: ﴿And He is the Almighty, the All-Wise﴾. Al-'Aziz is the Victorious who cannot be overcome, and al-Hakim is the One who places a thing in its proper place. So the attribute of greatness for Allah, the Most High, does not mean domination, tyranny, and arbitrary violence without restraint; rather, He, glory be to Him, is also All-Wise, who directs affairs according to absolute wisdom.

One who reflects on Surah al-Jathiya finds that it began with the saying of Allah, the Most High: ﴿Ha-Mim. The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Almighty, the All-Wise﴾ [al-Jathiya: 1-2], and it also ended with His saying, the Most High: ﴿And He is the Almighty, the All-Wise﴾.

It is as if the surah was placed between two brackets of might and wisdom belonging to Allah, the Most High, and of greatness and praise belonging to Allah, glory be to Him. And it is remarkable that al-Ahqaf, which follows it, also begins with the saying of Allah, the Most High: ﴿Ha-Mim. The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Almighty, the All-Wise﴾ [al-Jathiya: 1-2].

So Allah, the Most High, emphasizes these attributes and establishes them in the souls of the believers, to increase their tranquility in Him, glory be to Him, and in His method.

It is as if He, glory be to Him, were saying to them: "Be at peace. He who bestowed His blessings upon you in the past, by bringing you into existence from non-existence, and giving life to your substance with a spirit from Him, then supplied you with the means of life and its sustenance, and guided you to Himself through His signs that revive your hearts and grant you eternal life on the Day of Resurrection."

So He, glory be to Him, who guaranteed your past will guarantee your future. His blessings are not taken away, and His giving does not run out, because greatness in the heavens and the earth belongs to Him. No power other than Him, glory be to Him, can nullify this good or withhold it from you.

When Allah, the Most High, combines the two attributes of might and wisdom, it is only to tell us: "Be mindful: if events occur that seem to contradict this might in the course of the call (da'wa), know that they happened only for a wisdom."

Someone might say, for example: If Allah is Almighty and cannot be overcome, why did He leave His Messenger to the people of al-Ta'if, who harmed him, cursed him and pelted him with stones until his blessed feet bled?

We say: seek the wisdom. Among the wisdom intended by Allah, the Most High, when evil prevails, is that the people of goodness be tested and purified, and that the foundation of Islam be refined so that only the steadfast in faith, who hold firmly to the truth and do not turn away from it, remain. For upon the shoulders of these people the religion will be carried and the call will spread. Thus there must be testing and the distinguishing of believers from hypocrites...
